choices.text: The rectal mucosa regenerates faster than colonic mucosa

choices.label: E
choices.text: The rectum receives blood only from the mucosal surface rather than from the serosal side

explanation.summary: The rectum has a complete longitudinal muscle coat and therefore no weak points for herniation.
explanation.whyCorrect: As the sigmoid colon transitions to the rectum, the tenia coli converge into a continuous outer longitudinal muscle layer. Without the discrete tenia and their associated wall defects, the rectum is not prone to diverticulosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The rectum has a submucosa; the protective feature is its continuous outer longitudinal muscle coat.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Firm stool and segmentation raise pressure most in the sigmoid, but the anatomic reason the rectum is spared is its complete muscle layer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct. The converging tenia form a continuous longitudinal muscle layer, so the rectum does not develop diverticula.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucosal turnover has no bearing on herniation of mucosa and submucosa through a muscular defect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is not the explanation; sparing of the rectum is attributed to its complete outer longitudinal muscle layer.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man passes a large volume of bright red blood per rectum. He has no abdominal pain, no fever, and a soft, nontender abdomen. Urgent colonoscopy shows extensive sigmoid diverticulosis with an adherent clot at the mouth of one diverticulum; the cecum and right colon appear normal, and the mucosa elsewhere is normal. Which of the following best describes the source of this patient's bleeding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rupture of dilated, thin-walled mucosal and submucosal vessels in the cecum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Microperforation of an acutely inflamed diverticulum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mucosal ulceration of a watershed segment after transient hypoperfusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Arterial rupture at the neck of a diverticulum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mucosal shearing from twisting of the sigmoid colon around its mesentery

explanation.summary: Diverticular hemorrhage is painless arterial bleeding at the neck of a diverticulum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diverticular bleeding is a separate entity from diverticulitis and presents as painless, brisk hematochezia. It results from rupture of the artery that runs at the neck of the diverticulum, which is why the endoscopic stigma is found at the mouth of a pouch.

whyWrongByChoice.A: That describes angiodysplasia, but the cecum and right colon were normal and the stigma of bleeding was at a sigmoid diverticulum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Microperforation of a diverticulum defines diverticulitis, which causes pain, fever, and leukocytosis; rectal bleeding is not a feature of acute diverticulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ischemic colitis of a watershed segment causes pain followed by bloody diarrhea and shows ulcerated or dusky mucosa, not a normal-appearing colon with a clot on a diverticulum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct. Painless brisk hematochezia with a clot at a diverticular orifice reflects arterial rupture at the neck of the diverticulum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Volvulus produces closed-loop obstruction with distension and obstipation, not isolated painless hematochezia with an otherwise normal colon.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old woman with coronary artery disease develops sudden cramping left lower quadrant pain. Several hours later she begins passing bloody diarrhea. She is afebrile, and her abdomen is mildly tender in the left lower quadrant without peritoneal signs. CT of the abdomen shows wall thickening of the descending colon and rectosigmoid junction with pericolonic fat stranding. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute diverticulitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ischemic colitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Colonic angiodysplasia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sigmoid volvulus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Obstructing sigmoid carcinoma

explanation.summary: Left-sided pain followed rapidly by hematochezia points to ischemic colitis rather than diverticulitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ischemic colitis in an older adult classically causes acute abdominal pain followed within 24 hours by hematochezia or bloody diarrhea, and CT shows colonic wall thickening with pericolonic fat stranding. The watershed distribution described, involving the rectosigmoid junction, fits this diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rectal bleeding is not a feature of acute diverticulitis; left lower quadrant pain and tenderness combined with rectal bleeding indicate ischemic colitis instead.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct. Pain followed within hours by bloody diarrhea, in a watershed distribution with wall thickening and fat stranding, is ischemic colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Angiodysplasia causes painless bleeding and is concentrated in the cecum and right colon, without wall thickening or fat stranding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sigmoid volvulus causes closed-loop obstruction with marked distension and obstipation rather than bloody diarrhea with a thickened, inflamed wall.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An obstructing carcinoma presents insidiously with distension and obstipation, and late vomiting, not with acute pain followed by bloody diarrhea.

questions.stem: A 79-year-old woman has recurrent painless hematochezia and iron deficiency anemia. Endoscopic evaluation identifies acquired lesions consisting of dilated, thin-walled mucosal and submucosal blood vessels. These lesions are most commonly found in which of the following segments of the colon?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rectum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sigmoid colon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Splenic flexure of the colon

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mid portion of the transverse colon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cecum and ascending colon

explanation.summary: Colonic angiodysplasias cluster in the cecum and right colon.
explanation.whyCorrect: Angiodysplasias (angioectasias) are acquired dilated, thin-walled mucosal and submucosal vessels seen predominantly in elderly patients, and they occur most commonly in the cecum and right colon. Their presentation is painless bleeding, either occult loss with iron deficiency anemia or overt hematochezia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The rectum is not the characteristic site for angiodysplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The sigmoid is the characteristic site for diverticula and diverticulitis, not for angiodysplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The splenic flexure is a watershed area typically involved by ischemic colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The mid transverse colon is not the typical location of these vascular lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct. Angiodysplasias are most commonly located in the cecum and right colon.

questions.stem: An 82-year-old man has repeated episodes of painless hematochezia requiring transfusion. Colonoscopy identifies an actively bleeding cecal angiodysplasia. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Right hemicolectomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibiotics directed against gram-negative rods and anaerobes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endoscopic thermal coagulation with argon plasma coagulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Endoscopic decompression with placement of a rectal tube

choices.label: E
choices.text: CT-guided percutaneous drainage

explanation.summary: Bleeding angiodysplasia is first treated endoscopically with thermal coagulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: When an angiodysplasia requires treatment, endoscopic thermal coagulation such as argon plasma coagulation is first-line and can be applied at the time the lesion is identified. Most bleeding stops spontaneously, so intervention is directed at lesions that bleed significantly or repeatedly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Resection is not the first-line approach for a lesion accessible to endoscopic coagulation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibiotics against gram-negative rods and anaerobes treat diverticulitis, not a bleeding vascular lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct. Endoscopic thermal coagulation, for example argon plasma coagulation, is the first-line treatment for angiodysplasia requiring therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endoscopic decompression is the initial treatment of sigmoid volvulus, not of a bleeding vascular ectasia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Percutaneous drainage is used for a diverticular abscess, not for colonic bleeding.

questions.stem: A 77-year-old man has fatigue and a hemoglobin concentration of 8.9 g/dL with microcytic indices. Stool is positive for occult blood. Upper endoscopy and colonoscopy are both normal, with no diverticula, mass, or mucosal inflammation identified. Which of the following is the most likely source of his blood loss?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diverticular bleeding from the sigmoid colon

choices.label: B
choices.text: Angiodysplasia of the small intestine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ischemic colitis of the splenic flexure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chronic diverticulitis of the descending colon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adenocarcinoma of the descending colon

explanation.summary: Obscure GI bleeding in an older adult with normal endoscopy points to small bowel angiodysplasia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Angiodysplasias also occur in the small intestine, where they are the most common cause of obscure gastrointestinal bleeding in older adults. Their typical presentation is painless blood loss, either occult with iron deficiency anemia or overt hematochezia, and the small bowel is not visualized by standard upper endoscopy or colonoscopy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Colonoscopy showed no diverticula, and diverticular bleeding is brisk and overt rather than chronic occult loss.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct. Small intestinal angiodysplasia is the leading cause of obscure gastrointestinal bleeding in older adults and is missed by upper endoscopy and colonoscopy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ischemic colitis causes acute pain followed by hematochezia with visible mucosal injury on colonoscopy, none of which is present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Diverticulitis presents with pain, fever, and leukocytosis, and this patient has no diverticula and no pain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A colonic adenocarcinoma large enough to cause chronic blood loss would have been seen at colonoscopy.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old asymptomatic woman undergoes screening colonoscopy, which shows numerous diverticula in the sigmoid and descending colon. She feels well and has no abdominal pain or change in bowel habits. Which of the following best describes her expected clinical course?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nearly all patients with this finding go on to develop acute diverticulitis within 5 years

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most patients develop lower gastrointestinal bleeding requiring transfusion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most patients progress to a fibrotic sigmoid stricture with large-bowel obstruction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most patients remain asymptomatic; only 4 to 5 percent develop diverticulitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most patients ultimately require elective sigmoid colectomy

explanation.summary: Diverticulosis is common with age and is largely asymptomatic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diverticulosis becomes common with advancing age and is largely asymptomatic. Only about 4 to 5 percent of patients with diverticula ever develop diverticulitis, and the vast majority never require intervention.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Only a small minority, roughly 4 to 5 percent, ever develop diverticulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Most patients with diverticulosis never bleed, and when diverticular bleeding does occur it is self-limited in the overwhelming majority.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stricture is a complication of recurrent diverticulitis, which itself develops in only a small minority.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct. Diverticulosis is largely asymptomatic, with only about 4 to 5 percent of patients developing diverticulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Elective colectomy is considered only for selected patients with recurrent or severe episodes, not for asymptomatic diverticulosis.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man has recovered from an episode of uncomplicated diverticulitis. He asks whether he should permanently eliminate nuts, seeds, and popcorn from his diet to keep the pouches from becoming inflamed again. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoiding nuts, seeds, and popcorn is unnecessary because they do not raise risk

choices.label: B
choices.text: Popcorn kernels frequently lodge within diverticula and should be avoided for life

choices.label: C
choices.text: Seeds should be avoided, although nuts and popcorn are safe

choices.label: D
choices.text: All particulate foods should be avoided because they mechanically obstruct the diverticular neck

choices.label: E
choices.text: These foods should be avoided during the first year only, after which the risk normalizes

explanation.summary: The nut, seed, and popcorn restriction is a myth not supported by evidence.
explanation.whyCorrect: Large prospective studies show no increased risk of diverticulitis with nuts, seeds, or popcorn, and some studies show a decreased risk with popcorn intake, likely because of its fiber content. No popcorn kernel or seed has ever been observed inside an inflamed diverticulum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct. These foods do not increase risk, and restricting them is unnecessary.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Kernels have never been found in an inflamed diverticulum, and popcorn intake has not been shown to increase risk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Seeds are no more implicated than nuts or popcorn; none of the three increases risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mechanical obstruction of the diverticular neck by food particles is not the mechanism of diverticulitis, which is attributed to chronically elevated intraluminal pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There is no evidence-based interval of avoidance, because these foods do not raise risk at any time.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old woman has left lower quadrant pain, a temperature of 38.1 C (100.6 F), and a leukocyte count of 13,800/mm3. CT of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast shows sigmoid wall thickening and pericolic fat stranding with no abscess, free air, or obstruction. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Urgent sigmoid colectomy with end colostomy (Hartmann procedure)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibiotic therapy against gram-negative rods and anaerobes

choices.label: C
choices.text: CT-guided percutaneous catheter drainage

choices.label: D
choices.text: Endoscopic decompression of the sigmoid colon with rectal tube placement

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urgent colonoscopy with endoscopic clipping

explanation.summary: Uncomplicated diverticulitis is treated medically with appropriately targeted antibiotics.
explanation.whyCorrect: Her CT shows localized inflammation only, which defines uncomplicated diverticulitis, the pattern seen in roughly 85 percent of cases. Uncomplicated disease is treated with antibiotics covering gram-negative rods and anaerobes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Surgery is reserved for complicated disease such as perforation or peritonitis, or offered electively after recurrent episodes, not urgently for localized inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct. Uncomplicated diverticulitis is managed with antibiotics against gram-negative rods and anaerobes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Drainage is used when CT demonstrates an abscess, which is absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endoscopic decompression treats sigmoid volvulus, not diverticular inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endoscopic clipping targets a bleeding lesion; this patient has inflammation without bleeding.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man with left lower quadrant pain, fever, and leukocytosis undergoes CT of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast. It shows sigmoid wall thickening with adjacent diverticula and a 5-cm rim-enhancing pericolic fluid collection containing air. He is hemodynamically stable and has no diffuse peritonitis. In addition to antibiotics, which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discharge on oral antibiotics with outpatient follow-up

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endoscopic argon plasma coagulation of the inflamed segment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immediate initiation of a high-fiber diet

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nasogastric decompression and observation alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: CT-guided percutaneous drainage of the collection

explanation.summary: An abscess makes this complicated diverticulitis, which requires drainage.
explanation.whyCorrect: A rim-enhancing pericolic collection containing air is a diverticular abscess, placing this case in the complicated category along with perforation, fistula, obstruction, and stricture. Complicated diverticulitis requires drainage or surgery in addition to antibiotics.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Outpatient antibiotics alone are appropriate for uncomplicated disease; an abscess requires drainage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Argon plasma coagulation treats bleeding vascular lesions, not an infected collection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dietary measures have no role in treating an established abscess and have not been shown to prevent recurrence.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nasogastric decompression is used in bowel obstruction and does not address an abscess.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct. A diverticular abscess is complicated disease and is managed with drainage in addition to antibiotics.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman is admitted with acute diverticulitis. Which of the following CT findings would classify her disease as complicated rather than uncomplicated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wall thickening of the involved sigmoid segment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pericolic fat stranding adjacent to the inflamed segment

choices.label: C
choices.text: A rim-enhancing pericolic fluid collection containing air

choices.label: D
choices.text: Numerous diverticula throughout the descending colon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inflammation confined to the wall of a single sigmoid segment

explanation.summary: Complicated diverticulitis is defined by abscess, perforation, fistula, obstruction, or stricture.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uncomplicated diverticulitis, about 85 percent of cases, shows localized inflammation only. Complicated disease, about 12 to 15 percent, is defined by abscess, perforation, fistula, obstruction, or stricture, and a rim-enhancing air-containing collection is an abscess.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Wall thickening is part of the localized inflammation seen in uncomplicated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pericolic fat stranding reflects localized inflammation and does not by itself indicate complicated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct. An air-containing rim-enhancing collection is an abscess, which defines complicated diverticulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Background diverticulosis is the underlying anatomic finding and is not a complication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inflammation confined to the bowel wall is the definition of uncomplicated disease.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man has an episode of prolonged hypotension during cardiac surgery. Two days later he develops crampy abdominal pain followed by bloody diarrhea. Ischemic colitis is suspected. Which of the following segments is most likely to be involved?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cecum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ascending colon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hepatic flexure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Splenic flexure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Terminal ileum

explanation.summary: Ischemic colitis preferentially injures colonic watershed zones.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ischemic colitis results from transient reductions in colonic blood flow from hypoperfusion, vasospasm, or small-vessel occlusion, and it most often involves the watershed areas, the splenic flexure and the rectosigmoid junction. This patient's intraoperative hypotension is a classic low-flow trigger.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The cecum is the characteristic location of angiodysplasia, not of watershed ischemic injury.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The ascending colon is not a watershed zone for this process.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The hepatic flexure is not one of the described watershed areas.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct. The splenic flexure is a classic watershed area involved in ischemic colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The jejunum and ileum are the territory affected by acute mesenteric ischemia, which distinguishes it from ischemic colitis.

questions.stem: A 73-year-old woman develops abdominal pain followed several hours later by bloody diarrhea. She is hemodynamically stable, and her abdomen is mildly tender without peritoneal signs. Which of the following findings is most likely on CT of the abdomen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Colonic wall thickening with pericolonic fat stranding

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gas within the bowel wall of the small intestine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dilated small bowel loops with air-fluid levels and no colonic gas

choices.label: D
choices.text: A markedly dilated, coffee bean shaped loop arising from the pelvis

choices.label: E
choices.text: A massively distended stomach with minimal distal gas

explanation.summary: The CT appearance of ischemic colitis is colonic wall thickening with pericolonic fat stranding.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute abdominal pain followed within 24 hours by hematochezia or bloody diarrhea in an older adult is the classic presentation of ischemic colitis. On CT, this appears as colonic wall thickening with pericolonic fat stranding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct. Colonic wall thickening with pericolonic fat stranding is the expected CT appearance of ischemic colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intramural gas, pneumatosis intestinalis, is the pathognomonic radiographic finding of necrotizing enterocolitis in preterm neonates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dilated small bowel with air-fluid levels and absent colonic gas indicates small bowel obstruction, which presents with bilious vomiting and obstipation rather than bloody diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The coffee bean sign indicates sigmoid volvulus, a closed-loop obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A distended stomach with minimal distal gas indicates gastric outlet obstruction, which presents with vomiting and early satiety.

questions.stem: A 75-year-old man is admitted with abdominal pain followed by bloody diarrhea. CT shows segmental colonic wall thickening with pericolonic fat stranding at the splenic flexure. He is afebrile and hemodynamically stable, his abdomen is soft with mild tenderness, and there are no peritoneal signs. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Emergent segmental colectomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endoscopic argon plasma coagulation of the involved mucosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endoscopic decompression with a rectal tube

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elective sigmoid colectomy during this admission

choices.label: E
choices.text: Supportive care with bowel rest and intravenous fluids

explanation.summary: Most ischemic colitis is self-limited and treated supportively.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 85 percent of cases of ischemic colitis are self-limited and resolve with supportive care. Surgery is reserved for gangrenous disease, which risks perforation, sepsis, and death, and this patient has no peritoneal signs or hemodynamic instability.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Emergent resection is indicated for gangrenous disease, which is not present in this stable patient with a soft abdomen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Thermal coagulation treats discrete bleeding vascular lesions such as angiodysplasia, not diffuse ischemic mucosal injury.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Endoscopic decompression is the initial treatment of sigmoid volvulus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Elective sigmoid colectomy is considered for recurrent diverticulitis, not for an episode of ischemic colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct. Most cases are self-limited and resolve with supportive care.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man has had three prior episodes of sigmoid diverticulitis treated with antibiotics. Over the past 3 months he has had progressive constipation and abdominal distension. CT shows a narrowed sigmoid segment with dilated colon proximally. Colonoscopy shows a smooth, tapered narrowing surrounded by numerous diverticula, and biopsies show dense fibrosis without dysplasia or malignancy. Which of the following best explains his obstruction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Twisting of a redundant sigmoid colon around its mesenteric axis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fibrotic stricture from recurrent diverticulitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: An annular adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon

choices.label: D
choices.text: Telescoping of one bowel segment into the lumen of the adjacent segment

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transient hypoperfusion of a colonic watershed segment

explanation.summary: Recurrent diverticulitis can produce a fibrotic sigmoid stricture that obstructs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Stricture is one of the recognized complications of complicated diverticular disease. Chronic fibrosis from recurrent diverticulitis progressively narrows the sigmoid lumen and can mimic malignancy on imaging, which is why the endoscopic biopsies showing fibrosis without malignancy are decisive here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Volvulus causes sudden closed-loop obstruction with a dilated coffee bean shaped loop, not a fixed fibrotic narrowing with surrounding diverticula.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct. Recurrent diverticulitis produces chronic fibrosis that narrows the sigmoid and can mimic cancer on imaging.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Carcinoma is the most common cause of colonic obstruction overall and can look identical on CT, but biopsies here show fibrosis without malignancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intussusception in adults is uncommon and requires a pathologic lead point such as a polyp or tumor; it does not produce a fibrotic diverticular stricture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ischemic colitis presents acutely with pain and hematochezia and is usually self-limited rather than causing progressive mechanical obstruction.

questions.stem: An 80-year-old man is hospitalized for painless hematochezia. Colonoscopy identifies angiodysplasias in the cecum, and the bleeding stops without intervention before discharge. Which of the following best describes the expected subsequent course of bleeding from these lesions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bleeding almost always continues until surgical resection is performed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bleeding characteristically converts to painful bloody diarrhea over the following week

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bleeding stops spontaneously in most patients but frequently recurs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Once bleeding stops, recurrence is exceedingly rare

choices.label: E
choices.text: The lesions regress spontaneously and disappear on repeat colonoscopy

explanation.summary: Angiodysplastic bleeding is usually self-limited but recurrent.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bleeding from angiodysplasia stops spontaneously in about 85 percent of cases, which is why many patients need no immediate intervention. However, it often recurs, and endoscopic thermal coagulation is used when treatment becomes necessary.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Most episodes stop on their own; surgery is not required for hemostasis in the typical case.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pain followed by bloody diarrhea describes ischemic colitis; angiodysplastic bleeding is painless.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct. Bleeding stops spontaneously in most patients but often recurs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Recurrence is common, not rare, which is the reason these lesions are treated endoscopically when they bleed repeatedly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These are acquired structural vascular lesions that persist; they do not spontaneously disappear.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman with anorexia nervosa and a BMI of 14 kg/m2 is evaluated for 3 weeks of worsening epigastric pain that begins shortly after meals, along with early satiety and bilious vomiting. She has lost additional weight during this period. She denies self-induced vomiting, and her family confirms her account. She reports that her pain is worst when she lies flat on her back and improves when she lies on her left side. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ileocolic intussusception with a pathologic lead point

choices.label: C
choices.text: Superior mesenteric artery syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acute mesenteric ischemia from an arterial embolism

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sigmoid volvulus

explanation.summary: Rapid weight loss with postprandial pain, bilious vomiting, and positional relief is the classic presentation of SMA syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: SMA syndrome results from compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta after loss of the intervening fat pad, typically following rapid weight loss such as in an eating disorder. The hallmark features present here are postprandial epigastric pain, early satiety, bilious vomiting, and worsening of symptoms when supine with improvement in the left lateral decubitus position.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pyloric stenosis is a disease of infants at 3-6 weeks of age producing projectile nonbilious vomiting, not an adult with bilious vomiting.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intussusception peaks at 5-9 months of age with colicky pain, currant jelly stool, and a sausage-shaped mass; in adults it is uncommon and requires a pathologic lead point, none of which is described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: rapid weight loss narrows the aortomesenteric angle and compresses the duodenum, producing postprandial bilious vomiting that varies with position.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Acute mesenteric ischemia presents with sudden abdominal pain out of proportion to a benign examination, usually in older patients with atrial fibrillation or atherosclerosis, and progresses rapidly to peritonitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sigmoid volvulus occurs in elderly, institutionalized patients with chronic constipation and causes distension and obstipation, not postprandial epigastric pain relieved by position.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is hospitalized after losing 25 kg during treatment for extensive burns. He now has postprandial epigastric pain, early satiety, and bilious vomiting. CT of the abdomen with oral and intravenous contrast demonstrates a markedly narrowed aortomesenteric angle. Compression of which of the following structures best explains his symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pylorus by a hypertrophied ring of circular smooth muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Third portion of the duodenum beneath the superior mesenteric artery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Terminal ileum telescoped through the ileocecal valve into the cecum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sigmoid colon twisted around the narrow base of its redundant mesentery

choices.label: E
choices.text: Distal ileum by an adhesive band

explanation.summary: Tests the anatomic basis of SMA syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of the retroperitoneal fat pad after rapid weight loss narrows the aortomesenteric angle to less than 25 degrees, pinching the third portion of the duodenum where it crosses the midline between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta. The resulting proximal obstruction produces postprandial pain, early satiety, and bilious vomiting.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pyloric muscle hypertrophy causes gastric outlet obstruction in infants with nonbilious vomiting and is unrelated to the aortomesenteric angle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: the duodenum is compressed between the SMA and aorta once the intervening fat pad is lost.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Telescoping of the ileum into the colon describes intussusception, which would not produce a narrowed aortomesenteric angle on CT.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Twisting of the sigmoid around its mesentery is volvulus, a closed-loop colonic obstruction causing distension and obstipation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An adhesive band causes small bowel obstruction and requires prior abdominal surgery; it does not explain the CT finding of a narrowed aortomesenteric angle.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman with recent rapid weight loss has been diagnosed with compression of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta. She asks what she can do after meals to reduce her symptoms. Assuming which of the following positions is most likely to relieve her symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lying supine with the hips extended

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lying in the right lateral decubitus position

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reclining backward in a chair

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lying supine in the Trendelenburg position

choices.label: E
choices.text: Leaning forward in a knee-to-chest position

explanation.summary: Positional maneuvers relieve duodenal compression in SMA syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Symptoms of SMA syndrome worsen when the patient is supine and improve in the prone or left lateral decubitus position. Leaning forward in a knee-to-chest position after eating relieves compression of the third portion of the duodenum and is a recommended conservative measure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lying supine is the position that characteristically worsens symptoms of SMA syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Relief is described in the left lateral decubitus position, not the right.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reclining backward maintains the supine-type posture that aggravates duodenal compression rather than relieving it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trendelenburg positioning keeps the patient supine and offers no benefit for this obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: leaning forward in a knee-to-chest position after eating helps relieve the duodenal compression.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman with a BMI of 14 kg/m2 has postprandial epigastric pain and bilious vomiting. CT of the abdomen demonstrates compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery with a reduced aortomesenteric angle. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nutritional repletion to widen the aortomesenteric angle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Emergent operative bypass of the obstructed duodenal segment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Laparoscopic pyloromyotomy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Colonoscopic decompression with rectal tube placement

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intravenous antibiotics directed against enteric gram-negative rods and anaerobes

explanation.summary: SMA syndrome is treated first with nutritional rehabilitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the obstruction results from loss of the fat pad between the SMA and aorta, improved nutrition restores retroperitoneal fat and widens the angle, relieving the compression. Postural measures such as leaning forward after eating supplement this conservative approach.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: restoring nutrition rebuilds the retroperitoneal fat pad and widens the aortomesenteric angle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Surgical bypass of the obstruction is reserved for patients in whom conservative management fails, not as the initial step.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pyloromyotomy is the operation for infantile pyloric stenosis and does not address duodenal compression at the level of the SMA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Colonoscopic decompression is used for sigmoid volvulus, a colonic problem far distal to this obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibiotics for gram-negative rods and anaerobes treat diverticulitis or perioperative appendicitis; there is no infection here.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman with a recent 18-kg weight loss has postprandial epigastric pain, early satiety, and bilious vomiting. An upper gastrointestinal contrast series is obtained. Which of the following findings is most likely to be seen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contrast pooling in a massively distended stomach with delayed gastric emptying

choices.label: B
choices.text: Concentric target (donut) appearance of bowel within bowel on ultrasonography

choices.label: C
choices.text: A single massively dilated loop with a coffee bean configuration

choices.label: D
choices.text: Abrupt duodenal cutoff at the midline with proximal dilation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gas within the wall of the small intestine

explanation.summary: Upper GI findings of SMA syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: In SMA syndrome the upper GI series shows an abrupt duodenal cutoff with dilation of the duodenum and stomach proximal to it, corresponding to the point where the third portion of the duodenum crosses the midline between the aorta and the SMA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Contrast trapped in a distended stomach with no duodenal filling indicates gastric outlet obstruction at the pylorus or proximal duodenum, proximal to the site involved here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The target or donut sign is the ultrasound appearance of intussusception.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The coffee bean sign is the plain radiographic appearance of sigmoid volvulus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: an abrupt duodenal cutoff at the midline with proximal dilation is the classic upper GI finding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Intramural gas is pneumatosis intestinalis, the pathognomonic radiographic finding of necrotizing enterocolitis in preterm neonates.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with 2 days of colicky abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and obstipation. She underwent an abdominal hysterectomy 22 years ago. Her abdomen is distended and tympanitic with high-pitched bowel sounds and no rigidity. Abdominal radiographs show dilated air-filled loops of small intestine with air-fluid levels and no gas in the colon. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her obstruction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fibrotic stricture from Crohn disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Postoperative adhesions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gallstone impacted at the ileocecal valve

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obstructing colorectal carcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intussusception with a polyp lead point

explanation.summary: Adhesions are the most common cause of small bowel obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adhesions account for 60-75% of small bowel obstructions and can form after abdominal or pelvic surgery performed at any time in the past, even decades earlier. Her remote hysterectomy, colicky pain with bilious vomiting, and radiographs showing dilated small bowel with no colonic gas fit adhesive SBO.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Crohn disease accounts for only about 5% of small bowel obstructions and would be suggested by a history of chronic inflammatory bowel disease, which she lacks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: prior abdominal surgery makes adhesions by far the most likely cause.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gallstone ileus is a rare cause and would be accompanied by pneumobilia and an ectopic gallstone on imaging.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Colorectal cancer causes colonic obstruction with a dilated colon; here all dilated bowel is small intestine and no colonic gas is present.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adult intussusception is uncommon and requires a pathologic lead point such as a polyp or tumor; nothing here suggests one.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with no history of abdominal surgery presents with 18 hours of colicky abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, and obstipation. He has a firm, exquisitely tender bulge in the right groin that cannot be pushed back into the abdomen. Radiographs show dilated small bowel loops with air-fluid levels. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his obstruction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Postoperative adhesive band

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sigmoid volvulus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Radiation enteritis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Incarcerated inguinal hernia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Diverticular stricture of the sigmoid colon

explanation.summary: Hernia with incarcerated bowel is the second most common cause of small bowel obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hernias containing incarcerated intestine are the second most common cause of small bowel obstruction after adhesions. A tender groin bulge that cannot be reduced indicates incarceration, and surgical repair is emergent because of the risk of strangulation with loss of blood supply.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adhesions are the most common cause overall but require prior abdominal or pelvic surgery, which he has never had.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sigmoid volvulus produces a closed-loop colonic obstruction with marked distension in an elderly constipated patient, not an irreducible groin mass with dilated small bowel.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radiation enteritis is an uncommon cause and would follow prior abdominal or pelvic radiation, which is not described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: an irreducible, tender groin bulge with small bowel obstruction indicates an incarcerated inguinal hernia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A diverticular stricture narrows the sigmoid lumen and causes colonic obstruction, which would dilate the colon rather than only small bowel.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man presents with colicky abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, and distension. Supine and upright abdominal radiographs show multiple dilated loops of bowel with air-fluid levels and stair-stepping. Which of the following radiographic features best indicates that the dilated loops are small intestine rather than colon?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Closely spaced circular folds that traverse the full width of the bowel

choices.label: B
choices.text: Haustral markings about 1 cm apart that do not traverse the full width of the bowel

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gas within the wall of the bowel

choices.label: D
choices.text: Free air beneath the diaphragm on the upright film

choices.label: E
choices.text: A single markedly dilated loop with a coffee bean configuration

explanation.summary: Distinguishing small bowel from colon on plain abdominal radiographs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Small intestine is identified on plain film by its closely spaced circular folds that traverse the entire width of the bowel. Combined with air-fluid levels showing stair-stepping on the upright film and a lack of colonic gas, this establishes a small bowel obstruction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: closely spaced circular folds spanning the bowel width identify small intestine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Haustral markings roughly 1 cm apart that do not cross the full width identify colon, not small bowel.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intramural gas is pneumatosis intestinalis, a finding of necrotizing enterocolitis, and says nothing about which segment is dilated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Free air indicates perforation rather than identifying the level of bowel involved.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A single dilated loop with a coffee bean shape is characteristic of volvulus of the colon.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with prior abdominal surgery has colicky pain, bilious vomiting, distension, and obstipation. Plain radiographs suggest small bowel obstruction, and the surgical team wishes to define the site, cause, and severity of the obstruction and to assess whether the blood supply to the bowel is compromised. Which of the following is the most appropriate test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Upper gastrointestinal contrast series

choices.label: B
choices.text: Colonoscopy

choices.label: C
choices.text: CT of the abdomen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Abdominal ultrasound

choices.label: E
choices.text: Barium enema

explanation.summary: CT is the test of choice for small bowel obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: CT of the abdomen has become the test of choice for small bowel obstruction because it identifies the transition point, the cause, and the severity of the obstruction, and it can detect strangulation with compromised blood supply. Plain films only suggest the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An upper GI series is used to confirm the level of a proximal obstruction such as gastric outlet obstruction or SMA syndrome; it does not assess bowel perfusion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Colonoscopy is used to reach and identify the level of a colonic obstruction, not to evaluate obstructed small bowel.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: CT defines site, cause, and severity and detects strangulation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ultrasound is favored for suspected appendicitis in children and pregnant patients and for infantile pyloric stenosis, not for characterizing small bowel obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A contrast enema opacifies the colon and would not define a small bowel transition point or ischemia.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with a remote appendectomy presents with colicky abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, and distension. His abdomen is distended and tympanitic with mild diffuse tenderness but no rigidity or guarding. CT shows dilated small bowel with a transition point, normal bowel wall enhancement, and no free air. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Immediate exploratory laparotomy with bowel resection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Colonoscopic decompression with placement of a rectal tube

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hydrostatic contrast enema reduction under fluoroscopic guidance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Advancement to a regular diet as tolerated

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bowel rest, nasogastric decompression, and intravenous fluids

explanation.summary: Uncomplicated adhesive small bowel obstruction is managed nonoperatively at first.
explanation.whyCorrect: Initial management of adhesive small bowel obstruction is nonoperative with nothing by mouth, nasogastric decompression, and intravenous fluids; approximately 85% of cases resolve without surgery. His absent peritoneal signs and normally enhancing bowel argue against strangulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immediate operation is reserved for strangulation, peritonitis, failure to resolve, or an obstruction of unknown etiology; his prior appendectomy explains adhesions and he has no peritoneal signs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Colonoscopic decompression treats sigmoid volvulus, not adhesive small bowel obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hydrostatic or pneumatic enema reduction is used for pediatric intussusception.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Feeding an obstructed patient worsens proximal accumulation of gas and fluid and increases vomiting and aspiration risk.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: bowel rest, nasogastric decompression, and intravenous fluids resolve most adhesive obstructions.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman admitted 36 hours ago with an adhesive small bowel obstruction has been managed with nasogastric decompression and intravenous fluids. She now has a temperature of 38.9 C, a pulse of 124/min, and a rigid abdomen with involuntary guarding. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continue nasogastric suction for another 48 hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: Urgent surgical exploration

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeat abdominal radiographs in the morning

choices.label: D
choices.text: Begin oral feeding to test for resolution

choices.label: E
choices.text: Colonoscopic decompression

explanation.summary: Peritoneal signs during nonoperative management of SBO mandate urgent surgery.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peritoneal signs such as rigidity should be absent in uncomplicated small bowel obstruction; their appearance suggests strangulation or perforation and requires urgent surgical evaluation. Fever, tachycardia, and a rigid abdomen indicate that nonoperative management has failed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Continued nonoperative management risks progression of bowel ischemia to necrosis and sepsis once peritoneal signs appear.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: rigidity indicates strangulation or perforation and demands urgent operation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Delaying for repeat plain films adds no useful information and wastes time in a patient with peritonitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Feeding an obstructed patient with peritoneal signs is unsafe and does not address the surgical emergency.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Colonoscopic decompression addresses sigmoid volvulus and has no role in strangulated small bowel obstruction.

questions.stem: A 78-year-old woman presents with 3 days of colicky abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, and distension. CT of the abdomen and pelvis shows air within the biliary tree, distended small bowel loops, and a 3-cm calcified stone within the terminal ileum. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sigmoid volvulus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intussusception with a tumor lead point

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adhesive small bowel obstruction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gallstone ileus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cecal volvulus

explanation.summary: Rigler triad identifies gallstone ileus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rigler triad consists of pneumobilia, small bowel obstruction, and an ectopic gallstone within the intestine, all three of which are present. A large gallstone that erodes into the duodenum is propelled distally and impacts at the ileocecal valve, obstructing the small intestine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sigmoid volvulus obstructs the colon and would not produce pneumobilia or an intraluminal ileal stone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Adult intussusception requires a pathologic lead point such as a polyp or tumor and would not explain air in the biliary tree.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adhesive obstruction shows a transition point without an intraluminal stone or pneumobilia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: pneumobilia, SBO, and an ectopic gallstone constitute Rigler triad of gallstone ileus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cecal volvulus is a colonic closed-loop obstruction of younger patients and does not cause biliary air.

questions.stem: An 81-year-old woman with a long history of gallstones is found to have small bowel obstruction caused by a large gallstone impacted at the ileocecal valve. Which of the following best explains how the stone entered the intestinal tract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The stone eroded through the gallbladder wall into the duodenum

choices.label: B
choices.text: The stone passed through the common bile duct and ampulla of Vater into the duodenum

choices.label: C
choices.text: The gallbladder ruptured into the peritoneal cavity and spilled stones into the bowel

choices.label: D
choices.text: A pancreatic duct stone eroded directly into the proximal jejunum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bile salts precipitated within the ileal lumen to form the stone in situ

explanation.summary: Gallstone ileus requires a cholecystoenteric fistula.
explanation.whyCorrect: In gallstone ileus a large gallstone erodes through the gallbladder wall into the duodenum, creating a cholecystoenteric fistula. The stone is then propelled distally and, if large, impacts at the ileocecal valve; the fistula also explains the pneumobilia seen on imaging.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: erosion into the duodenum through a cholecystoenteric fistula delivers the stone into the bowel.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A stone large enough to obstruct at the ileocecal valve cannot traverse the common bile duct and ampulla.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Free rupture into the peritoneal cavity would not place a stone inside the bowel lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The stone in gallstone ileus originates in the gallbladder, not the pancreatic duct.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gallstones form in the gallbladder; they do not precipitate de novo within the ileal lumen.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man reports 2 weeks of progressive abdominal distension and obstipation, with vomiting beginning only yesterday. Abdominal radiographs show a dilated colon with no gas beyond the mid descending colon. CT of the abdomen and pelvis with rectal contrast shows a short segment of tight concentric narrowing in the descending colon through which contrast does not pass proximally. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his obstruction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adhesions from prior abdominal surgery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sigmoid volvulus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fibrostenotic Crohn disease stricture

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gallstone ileus

explanation.summary: Colorectal cancer is the most common cause of colonic obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Colorectal cancer is the most common cause of mechanical colonic obstruction, particularly in the distal colon where the smaller lumen produces obstruction earlier. The insidious onset with early distension and obstipation, late vomiting, and a tight annular narrowing that blocks rectal contrast is characteristic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adhesions are the leading cause of small bowel obstruction, not of a focal annular narrowing of the descending colon.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sigmoid volvulus produces a massively dilated twisted loop with a coffee bean appearance rather than a short segment of fixed concentric narrowing.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Crohn disease causes small bowel obstruction from inflammatory edema or fibrotic strictures and accounts for only a small share of obstructions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: an obstructing annular lesion of the distal colon in an older adult is most likely adenocarcinoma, the most common cause of colonic obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gallstone ileus obstructs the small intestine at the ileocecal valve and is accompanied by pneumobilia and an ectopic stone.

questions.stem: A surgical team is reviewing the causes of mechanical large bowel obstruction in adults. Which of the following is the most common benign cause of colonic obstruction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diverticular stricture

choices.label: C
choices.text: Crohn disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Postoperative adhesions

choices.label: E
choices.text: Volvulus

explanation.summary: Volvulus leads the benign causes of colonic obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the causes of colonic obstruction, volvulus is the most common benign etiology, and sigmoid volvulus predominates. It produces a closed-loop obstruction from twisting of the bowel around its mesenteric axis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Colorectal cancer is the most common cause of colonic obstruction overall, but it is a malignancy rather than a benign cause.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Diverticular stricture from chronic fibrosis after recurrent diverticulitis causes colonic obstruction but is less common than volvulus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Crohn disease accounts for roughly 5% of obstructions and does so mainly in the small intestine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adhesions are the dominant cause of small bowel obstruction, not colonic obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: volvulus, most often sigmoid, is the most common benign cause of large bowel obstruction.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman has a mechanical obstruction of the sigmoid colon. CT shows a dilated colon proximal to the lesion and a competent ileocecal valve preventing decompression into the small bowel; the cecum measures 10 cm in diameter. Which of the following complications is most likely if the obstruction is not relieved?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Perforation of the stomach

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perforation of the cecum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perforation of the duodenum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perforation of the rectum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Perforation of the jejunum

explanation.summary: Closed-loop colonic obstruction threatens the cecum because of Laplace's law.
explanation.whyCorrect: When the ileocecal valve is competent, colonic obstruction becomes a closed loop that cannot decompress into the small intestine. By Laplace's law the cecum, which has the largest diameter, develops the highest wall tension and is most prone to perforation; a cecal diameter greater than 9 cm is concerning.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The stomach lies proximal to the closed loop and is decompressed by vomiting and nasogastric suction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: the largest-diameter segment, the cecum, bears the greatest wall tension and perforates first.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The duodenum is not part of the closed loop created by a competent ileocecal valve.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The rectum lies distal to the obstruction and is decompressed rather than distended.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A competent ileocecal valve protects the jejunum from the rising colonic pressure.

questions.stem: An 84-year-old nursing home resident with chronic constipation is brought in with 3 days of progressive abdominal distension and obstipation. His abdomen is markedly distended and tympanitic. Abdominal radiography shows a single massively dilated loop of bowel with a coffee bean configuration whose fold points toward the left lower quadrant. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cecal volvulus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ileocolic intussusception

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obstructing rectal carcinoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sigmoid volvulus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Diverticular stricture

explanation.summary: Coffee bean sign in an elderly institutionalized patient indicates sigmoid volvulus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sigmoid volvulus is the most common type of volvulus and occurs in elderly, institutionalized patients with chronic constipation and a redundant sigmoid colon. The classic radiographic finding is the coffee bean sign, whose fold points down toward the left lower quadrant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cecal volvulus occurs in younger patients, and its coffee bean appearance is less common and points in the opposite direction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intussusception peaks in infancy with colicky pain and a target sign on ultrasound; in adults it requires a pathologic lead point.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An obstructing carcinoma produces a dilated colon proximal to a fixed narrowing rather than a single twisted coffee bean loop.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: the demographics and coffee bean sign pointing to the left lower quadrant indicate sigmoid volvulus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A diverticular stricture narrows the sigmoid lumen through chronic fibrosis and does not create a massively twisted single loop.

questions.stem: An 80-year-old man with chronic constipation has abdominal distension and obstipation. CT of the abdomen confirms sigmoid volvulus without evidence of ischemia or perforation. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endoscopic decompression

choices.label: B
choices.text: Emergent sigmoid resection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pneumatic enema reduction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nasogastric decompression alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Percutaneous drainage

explanation.summary: Sigmoid volvulus is initially treated endoscopically.
explanation.whyCorrect: Initial treatment of sigmoid volvulus is endoscopic decompression, which untwists and decompresses the closed loop. Elective sigmoid resection is then performed to prevent recurrence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: endoscopic decompression is the initial treatment for sigmoid volvulus without ischemia or perforation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sigmoid resection is performed electively after decompression rather than emergently in an uncomplicated case.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pneumatic enema reduction is used for pediatric intussusception.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nasogastric decompression addresses proximal gas and fluid but cannot relieve a twisted closed-loop colonic obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Percutaneous drainage treats a diverticular abscess, not a volvulus.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man presents with abdominal distension and obstipation. CT of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrates a cecal volvulus with a closed-loop obstruction and no evidence of perforation. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Colonoscopic decompression followed by observation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrostatic enema reduction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Surgical intervention

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nasogastric decompression and serial examinations

choices.label: E
choices.text: Antibiotics directed at gram-negative rods and anaerobes

explanation.summary: Cecal volvulus requires an operation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cecal volvulus occurs in younger patients and requires surgical intervention because endoscopic decompression is ineffective for this location. Leaving the closed loop untreated risks ischemia and perforation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Endoscopic decompression works for sigmoid volvulus but is ineffective for cecal volvulus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hydrostatic enema reduction is a treatment for pediatric intussusception.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: cecal volvulus is managed surgically because endoscopic decompression does not work.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Watchful waiting with nasogastric suction leaves a closed-loop obstruction untreated and risks perforation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibiotics alone treat uncomplicated diverticulitis and do not relieve a mechanical closed-loop obstruction.

questions.stem: A group of physicians is comparing the clinical presentations of small bowel and colonic obstruction. Which of the following features is most characteristic of colonic obstruction relative to small bowel obstruction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Profuse bilious vomiting beginning within the first few hours of symptom onset

choices.label: B
choices.text: Abrupt onset of severe colicky symptoms over several hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: Absence of abdominal distension at any point during the illness course

choices.label: D
choices.text: Painless brisk hematochezia as the initial presenting symptom

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gradual onset with early distension and obstipation, vomiting late

explanation.summary: Colonic obstruction presents more insidiously than small bowel obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Compared with small bowel obstruction, colonic obstruction develops more insidiously, with early abdominal distension and obstipation, while vomiting is a late finding. Colonic obstruction also accounts for only about 25% of mechanical bowel obstructions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Early bilious vomiting is typical of small bowel obstruction; in colonic obstruction vomiting appears late.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An abrupt course over hours is more typical of small bowel obstruction or strangulation than of colonic obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Abdominal distension is prominent and occurs early in colonic obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Painless brisk hematochezia describes diverticular bleeding, not mechanical colonic obstruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: insidious onset with early distension and obstipation and late vomiting characterizes colonic obstruction.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman undergoes a screening colonoscopy. In the sigmoid colon the endoscopist identifies a 9-mm mucosal protuberance projecting into the lumen. The base of the lesion has a distinctly smaller diameter than its rounded top, so that the lesion appears to hang into the lumen on a stalk. Which of the following terms best describes the gross morphology of this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Annular and circumferential

choices.label: B
choices.text: Depressed

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pedunculated

choices.label: D
choices.text: Flat

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sessile and broad-based

explanation.summary: Gross classification of intestinal polyps as flat, sessile, or pedunculated is based on the degree of protrusion and the presence of a stalk.
explanation.whyCorrect: A polyp whose base has a smaller diameter than its top is pedunculated: the narrow base forms a stalk from which the head of the polyp hangs into the lumen. This is the classic mushroom-like appearance described endoscopically.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Annular describes a circumferential constricting lesion of the bowel wall, not a stalked mucosal protuberance projecting into the lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Depressed lesions sit at or below the level of the surrounding mucosa and by definition have no stalk and little protrusion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: a base of smaller diameter than the top defines a pedunculated polyp, which hangs into the lumen on a stalk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A flat polyp shows minimal protrusion into the lumen and no stalk, which is the opposite of the lesion described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A sessile polyp has a base and a top of the same diameter, meaning it is broad based without a stalk.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man undergoes a screening colonoscopy. A single 4-mm polyp is found incidentally in the descending colon and removed. Histologic sections show mature goblet cells and absorptive cells with irregular tufting of the surface epithelium; the crowding of epithelial cells produces a serrated contour in the upper portion of the crypts, while the crypt bases are straight and unremarkable. There is no nuclear hyperchromasia or crowding. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inflammatory pseudopolyp

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hyperplastic polyp

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sessile serrated polyp

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tubular adenoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Villous adenoma

explanation.summary: Hyperplastic polyps are small left-sided benign epithelial proliferations of mature goblet and absorptive cells with serrated surface architecture.
explanation.whyCorrect: This lesion is small (under 5 mm), located in the left colon, and composed of mature goblet and absorptive cells whose overcrowding produces surface tufting and a serrated profile. That combination in a patient in the sixth to seventh decade is the classic description of a hyperplastic polyp, which lacks malignant potential.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inflammatory pseudopolyps arise from repeated cycles of mucosal injury and healing, typically in inflammatory bowel disease, and would occur in a background of erosion and inflammation rather than as an incidental isolated polyp.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: mature goblet and absorptive cells with a serrated surface in a small left colon polyp define a hyperplastic polyp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sessile serrated polyps overlap histologically with hyperplastic polyps but are more commonly right sided and show serration along the full length of the gland including the crypt base, with crypt dilation and lateral crypt extension, none of which is present here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A tubular adenoma shows dysplastic glands with crowded hyperchromatic nuclei and loss of goblet cells, whereas this polyp contains mature goblet cells without atypia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A villous adenoma is a dysplastic neoplasm with long finger-like fronds; this lesion has neither villous architecture nor dysplasia.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man at average risk for colorectal cancer undergoes his first screening colonoscopy. A single 3-mm polyp in the sigmoid colon is removed; pathology shows a hyperplastic polyp. The remainder of the examination is normal, and he has no family history of colorectal cancer. Which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation regarding his next colonoscopy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Repeat colonoscopy in 6 months

choices.label: B
choices.text: Repeat colonoscopy in 1 year

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeat colonoscopy in 3 years

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat colonoscopy in 5 years

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat colonoscopy in 10 years

explanation.summary: A hyperplastic polyp has no malignant potential and does not shorten the colonoscopy surveillance interval.
explanation.whyCorrect: Finding a hyperplastic polyp on colonoscopy does not change the frequency of subsequent colonoscopies. This patient therefore remains on the average-risk schedule of colonoscopy every 10 years.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 6-month interval is not indicated for a lesion without malignant potential and no other abnormal findings.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Shortened intervals of 1 to 7 years apply after removal of adenomatous polyps, not hyperplastic polyps.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 3-year interval would imply that a precancerous lesion had been removed, which is not the case here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A 5-year interval also reflects post-adenoma surveillance; a hyperplastic polyp does not alter the screening schedule.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: because a hyperplastic polyp does not change screening frequency, he continues average-risk colonoscopy every 10 years.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with a 10-year history of ulcerative colitis undergoes colonoscopy for worsening bloody diarrhea. The descending colon shows confluent mucosal erosions, and between the eroded areas there are numerous slender polypoid mucosal projections. Biopsies of the projections show regenerating mucosa with inflammation and no dysplasia. Which of the following best explains the formation of these lesions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Repeated cycles of mucosal injury and healing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clonal epithelial proliferation with high-grade dysplasia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Overgrowth of smooth muscle bundles extending through the lamina propria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Epithelial overcrowding producing serrated crypt architecture

choices.label: E
choices.text: Germline inactivation of a tumor suppressor gene

explanation.summary: Inflammatory pseudopolyps in inflammatory bowel disease result from repeated injury and healing around areas of mucosal erosion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inflammatory polyps usually form because of repeated cycles of injury and healing. In inflammatory bowel disease, mucosal erosion leaves islands of regenerating mucosa that project into the lumen as inflammatory pseudopolyps, exactly as described here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: repeated injury and healing with mucosal erosion produces the inflammatory pseudopolyps seen in inflammatory bowel disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The biopsies show no dysplasia, so a dysplastic clonal neoplastic proliferation does not explain these lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Smooth muscle bundles cutting through the lamina propria characterize hamartomatous Peutz-Jeghers polyps, not inflammatory pseudopolyps.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Epithelial overcrowding with serrated architecture describes hyperplastic polyps, which are unrelated to the ulcerated inflammatory background here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A germline tumor suppressor mutation underlies hereditary polyposis syndromes such as familial adenomatous polyposis, not reactive polyps arising in colitis.

questions.stem: An 11-year-old boy is evaluated for intermittent crampy abdominal pain and iron deficiency anemia. Physical examination shows dark blue to brown macules on the lips, nostrils, buccal mucosa, and palmar surfaces of the hands. Upper endoscopy and capsule study reveal multiple polyps in the small intestine and a smaller number in the colon and stomach. Histology of a resected jejunal polyp shows an arborizing network of smooth muscle bundles cutting through the lamina propria beneath a normal-appearing epithelial surface. A mutation in which of the following genes is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: APC

choices.label: B
choices.text: MLH1

choices.label: C
choices.text: SMAD4

choices.label: D
choices.text: STK11

choices.label: E
choices.text: MUTYH

explanation.summary: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is an autosomal dominant hamartomatous polyposis syndrome caused by STK11 mutations.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation as dark blue to brown macules of the lips, nostrils, buccal mucosa, and palms combined with multiple gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps that are most numerous in the small intestine is Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. It is a rare autosomal dominant condition caused by mutations in STK11 and typically presents in childhood around a median age of 11 years.

whyWrongByChoice.A: APC mutations cause familial adenomatous polyposis, which produces hundreds of adenomatous colorectal polyps rather than small intestinal hamartomas with mucocutaneous pigmentation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MLH1 is a mismatch repair gene mutated in Lynch syndrome, which is characterized by colorectal cancer, especially of the right colon, not by hamartomatous polyps or pigmented macules.
whyWrongByChoice.C: SMAD4 mutations cause juvenile polyposis syndrome, which produces hamartomatous polyps but is not associated with mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: pigmented macules plus small intestine predominant hamartomatous polyps in a child indicate Peutz-Jeghers syndrome from an STK11 mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MUTYH mutations cause an autosomal recessive polyposis syndrome with 10 to 100 adenomatous colorectal polyps, not hamartomas with pigmented macules.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of recurrent abdominal pain. Examination shows dark brown macules on the vermilion border of the lips and in the perianal region. Endoscopy reveals multiple polyps throughout the jejunum and ileum, and one is resected. Which of the following is the most likely histologic finding in the resected polyp?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Back-to-back malignant glands infiltrating the muscularis propria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bundles of smooth muscle arborizing through the lamina propria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mature goblet and absorptive cells with surface serration

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serrated architecture along the entire crypt length with crypt dilation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Long villous fronds lined by cells with high-grade dysplasia

explanation.summary: Peutz-Jeghers polyps are hamartomas whose defining histologic feature is smooth muscle cutting through the lamina propria.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pigmented macules of the lips and perianal skin with multiple small intestinal polyps indicate Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Its hamartomatous polyps show an epithelial surface overlying stroma composed of smooth muscle bundles cutting through the lamina propria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Malignant glands invading the muscularis propria define invasive adenocarcinoma, not the benign hamartoma of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: Peutz-Jeghers polyps are hamartomas with stromal smooth muscle bundles cutting through the lamina propria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mature goblet and absorptive cells with surface serration describe a colonic hyperplastic polyp, which is unrelated to this syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Full-length crypt serration with crypt dilation defines a sessile serrated polyp of the colon, not a small intestinal hamartoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Villous fronds with high-grade dysplasia describe a high-risk adenomatous polyp, whereas Peutz-Jeghers polyps are hamartomatous rather than dysplastic.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old boy has just been diagnosed with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome after presenting with pigmented macules of the lips and multiple small intestinal hamartomatous polyps. His parents ask what this means for his long-term cancer risk and what monitoring he will need. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is no increased cancer risk; he should begin routine average-risk screening at age 45 years

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cancer risk is increased only after age 50 years, so surveillance can begin then

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immediate prophylactic total colectomy is required to prevent colorectal cancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: His lifetime cancer risk approaches 40%, and surveillance should begin now

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surveillance is indicated only if he develops gastrointestinal bleeding or obstruction

explanation.summary: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome carries a high malignancy risk that mandates lifelong surveillance beginning in childhood.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome carries a high malignancy risk of approximately 40%. Because the syndrome presents in childhood, surveillance must be lifelong and must begin in childhood rather than at the age at which average-risk screening would ordinarily start.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome confers a substantially increased cancer risk, so deferring to the average-risk screening age of 45 years is inappropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Waiting until age 50 years ignores that surveillance in this syndrome is meant to start in childhood.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prophylactic colectomy is a consideration in familial adenomatous polyposis, not a standard requirement for hamartomatous Peutz-Jeghers polyps.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: the roughly 40% malignancy risk requires lifelong surveillance starting in childhood.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surveillance is intended to detect disease before symptoms develop; waiting for bleeding or obstruction defeats its purpose.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old boy is evaluated for rectal bleeding and fatigue. Colonoscopy reveals numerous polyps throughout the colon and rectum, and histology shows hamartomatous polyps. Genetic testing identifies a germline mutation in SMAD4. His father underwent surgery for intestinal polyps at a young age. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cerebral medulloblastoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation of the lips and buccal mucosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Osteomas of the skull

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sebaceous neoplasms of the skin

explanation.summary: Juvenile polyposis syndrome from SMAD4 mutation is associated with congenital malformations, notably pulmonary arteriovenous malformations.
explanation.whyCorrect: Numerous hamartomatous polyps with a SMAD4 mutation and an affected parent indicate autosomal dominant juvenile polyposis syndrome. These patients also have various congenital malformations, of which pulmonary arteriovenous malformations are the classic example.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Medulloblastoma occurs in Turcot syndrome, which features adenomatous colonic polyps rather than hamartomatous polyps with a SMAD4 mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dark blue to brown mucocutaneous macules are the hallmark of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, which is caused by STK11 rather than SMAD4 mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Skull osteomas are seen in Gardner syndrome, a subtype of familial adenomatous polyposis with adenomatous polyps.
