whyWrongByChoice.A: Internal hemorrhoidal disease presents with painless bleeding or prolapse and has no role in fissure non-healing.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Obstructed anal glands produce abscesses and fistulas; fissure non-healing is due to spasm-induced ischemia rather than glandular infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The anoderm retains its somatic innervation, which is precisely why fissures are so painful and why the reflex spasm is triggered.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pudendal stretch injury is not the mechanism described for poor fissure healing; sphincter spasm and posterior midline ischemia are.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: reflex internal sphincter spasm reduces blood flow in the already poorly perfused posterior midline, impairing healing.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man has had drainage from a small perianal opening for 3 months following drainage of a perianal abscess. In the operating room, the tract is probed and found to be simple and superficial, coursing beneath only a minimal amount of sphincter muscle. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prolonged oral antibiotic therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fistulotomy, laying the tract open

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lateral internal sphincterotomy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat incision and drainage of the external opening

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical nifedipine ointment

explanation.summary: Simple, low fistulas are treated by laying the tract open.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment of fistula-in-ano is surgical, and fistulotomy, laying open the tract, is the procedure for simple, low fistulas. Because minimal sphincter muscle is involved, laying the tract open carries little risk to continence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotics do not close an epithelialized chronic tract; fistulas require surgical treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: a simple, low fistula with minimal sphincter involvement is treated with fistulotomy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lateral internal sphincterotomy is the operation for medically refractory chronic anal fissure, not for a fistula tract.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Repeat drainage of the external opening does not eliminate the tract or the persistent internal opening that sustains it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Topical calcium channel blockers relax internal sphincter spasm in fissures and have no effect on a fistula tract.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man presents with 1 week of anorectal pain and a persistent sensation of needing to move his bowels even immediately after defecating. He also reports mucopurulent rectal discharge. He reports receptive anal intercourse with new partners over the past several months. There is no palpable perianal mass and no fluctuance or induration. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anal fissure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Infectious proctitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Thrombosed external hemorrhoid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perianal abscess

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prolapsing internal hemorrhoid

explanation.summary: This item tests recognition of infectious proctitis by its classic triad of anorectal pain, tenesmus, and mucopurulent or bloody rectal discharge in a patient with receptive anal intercourse.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infectious proctitis occurs predominantly in patients who practice receptive anal intercourse and presents with anorectal pain, tenesmus, and mucopurulent or bloody rectal discharge. This patient has all three symptoms plus the characteristic exposure history, and there are no findings of a structural anorectal lesion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An anal fissure is a tear in the anoderm that causes sharp, tearing pain during defecation with a small amount of bright red blood, not mucopurulent discharge with tenesmus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: anorectal pain, tenesmus, and mucopurulent discharge in a patient with receptive anal intercourse is the classic presentation of infectious proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A thrombosed external hemorrhoid causes sudden, severe perianal pain with a firm, tender, bluish lump at the anal verge; no such mass is present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A perianal abscess causes constant, throbbing perianal pain with swelling, erythema, and often a fluctuant mass or focal firmness, none of which is described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolapsing internal hemorrhoids cause painless bright red bleeding and protruding mucosa-covered tissue, not painful mucopurulent discharge.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man reports 10 days of anorectal pain, tenesmus, and bloody mucus per rectum. He has receptive anal intercourse and has not been tested for sexually transmitted infections. Anoscopy shows an inflamed, friable rectal mucosa without a mass. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nucleic acid testing for gonorrhea and chlamydia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scotch tape test of the perianal skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Examination under anesthesia in the operating room

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stool testing for ova and parasites

choices.label: E
choices.text: Anoscopic grading of internal hemorrhoids by degree of prolapse

explanation.summary: This item tests the diagnostic evaluation of suspected infectious proctitis, which begins with nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) for gonorrhea and chlamydia along with HSV testing and syphilis serology.
explanation.whyCorrect: The presentation of anorectal pain, tenesmus, and bloody mucopurulent discharge in a patient with receptive anal intercourse points to infectious proctitis. Evaluation of these patients includes NAAT for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis, HSV testing, and syphilis serology.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: NAAT for gonorrhea and chlamydia is part of the standard initial evaluation of infectious proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The Scotch tape test collects pinworm eggs from the perianal skin and is used for nocturnal perianal pruritus, not for rectal inflammation with discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Examination under anesthesia is used when a deep anorectal abscess is suspected but cannot be identified externally; this patient has visible mucosal inflammation, not an abscess.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stool ova and parasite testing does not target the organisms responsible for infectious proctitis in this setting.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Grading internal hemorrhoids addresses bleeding and prolapse, not an inflamed friable rectal mucosa with purulent discharge.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has 6 weeks of rectal bleeding, urgency, and tenesmus. Colonoscopy shows inflamed, granular, friable mucosa confined to the rectum with normal mucosa proximally, and biopsies confirm ulcerative colitis limited to the rectum. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rubber band ligation of internal hemorrhoids

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mesalamine suppositories

choices.label: C
choices.text: Topical nitroglycerin ointment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lateral internal sphincterotomy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Incision and drainage of a perianal abscess

explanation.summary: This item tests first-line therapy for ulcerative proctitis, which is topical mesalamine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ulcerative proctitis is ulcerative colitis limited to the rectum and presents with rectal bleeding, urgency, and tenesmus. First-line treatment is topical mesalamine (5-ASA suppositories), which works well because the inflammation is localized to the rectum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rubber band ligation is the office procedure for symptomatic internal hemorrhoids that fail conservative therapy, not for inflammatory rectal mucosal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: topical mesalamine suppositories are first-line for ulcerative proctitis given the localized nature of the inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Topical nitroglycerin relaxes internal sphincter spasm in anal fissures and has no role in mucosal inflammation of the rectum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lateral internal sphincterotomy permanently reduces resting internal sphincter tone for refractory chronic anal fissures, not for ulcerative proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Incision and drainage treats a perianal abscess; there is no abscess in this patient.

questions.stem: A student is reviewing the distribution of disease at the time of initial diagnosis in patients with ulcerative colitis. Disease limited to the rectum (ulcerative proctitis) accounts for approximately which of the following proportions of new ulcerative colitis diagnoses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fewer than 5%

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 10%

choices.label: C
choices.text: Up to 40%

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 70%

choices.label: E
choices.text: More than 90%

explanation.summary: This item tests the frequency of ulcerative proctitis among newly diagnosed ulcerative colitis patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ulcerative proctitis is a form of ulcerative colitis limited to the rectum and accounts for up to 40% of new ulcerative colitis diagnoses. This is why rectal bleeding, urgency, and tenesmus are common initial presentations of ulcerative colitis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This substantially underestimates how often new ulcerative colitis is confined to the rectum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This underestimates the proportion; rectal-limited disease is far more common than one in ten new diagnoses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: up to 40% of new ulcerative colitis diagnoses are limited to the rectum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This overestimates the proportion; most new diagnoses are not limited to the rectum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nearly all new ulcerative colitis diagnoses being rectal-limited would be inconsistent with the recognized proportion.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman with proctitis reports a constant, uncomfortable urge to move her bowels. She strains repeatedly but passes only small amounts of mucus, and digital rectal examination reveals an empty rectal vault. Which of the following best explains her symptom?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inflammation stimulates rectal sensory nerves and triggers muscle spasm

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reflex internal sphincter spasm follows a tear in the somatically innervated anoderm, reducing mucosal blood flow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obstruction of anal glands at the dentate line spreads infection into adjacent spaces

choices.label: D
choices.text: Degradation of the connective tissue supporting the anal vascular cushions permits prolapse

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of resting internal anal sphincter tone impairs continence

explanation.summary: This item tests the mechanism of tenesmus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Inflammation, irritation, or distention of the rectum abnormally stimulates rectal sensory nerves and triggers spasmodic contractions of the rectal and pelvic floor muscles. This produces a persistent urge to evacuate even when the rectum is empty, which is precisely what this patient describes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: rectal inflammation stimulates rectal sensory nerves and provokes spasmodic rectal and pelvic floor contractions, generating tenesmus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reflex sphincter spasm after an anoderm tear describes the pain-spasm-ischemia cycle of an anal fissure, which causes sharp pain with defecation rather than a persistent urge with an empty rectum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anal gland obstruction with spread of infection describes the origin of perianal abscess and fistula, which cause throbbing pain and drainage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Connective tissue degradation underlies internal hemorrhoid prolapse, which causes painless bleeding and protruding tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reduced internal sphincter tone relates to continence problems, not to a persistent urge to evacuate.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy is brought in because of intense perianal itching that wakes him from sleep most nights. He is otherwise well, and the perianal skin shows only excoriations. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Colonoscopy with rectal biopsy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Punch biopsy of the perianal skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Syphilis serology

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scotch tape test of the perianal skin in the early morning

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nucleic acid amplification testing for gonorrhea and chlamydia

explanation.summary: This item tests the diagnostic approach to suspected enterobiasis (pinworm infection) as a cause of pruritus ani.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nocturnal perianal pruritus in a school-age child is classic for enterobiasis, which results from nighttime deposition of pinworm eggs around the anus. Diagnosis is made with the Scotch tape test performed in the early morning to collect eggs for microscopic examination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Colonoscopy with biopsy diagnoses ulcerative proctitis, which presents with rectal bleeding, urgency, and tenesmus rather than nocturnal perianal itching.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Skin biopsy is directed at persistent or refractory perianal lesions in which neoplasia must be excluded, not at a child with classic nocturnal itching.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Syphilis serology is part of the evaluation of infectious proctitis, which presents with anorectal pain, tenesmus, and discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: the early-morning Scotch tape test collects perianal pinworm eggs for microscopic identification.
whyWrongByChoice.E: NAAT for gonorrhea and chlamydia is used for suspected infectious proctitis, not for pruritus ani in a child.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl has 3 weeks of perianal itching that is worst at night. Her younger brother has similar symptoms. Microscopic examination of material collected from the perianal skin in the early morning shows numerous ovoid eggs. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human papillomavirus type 6

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enterobius vermicularis

explanation.summary: This item tests identification of Enterobius vermicularis as the cause of nocturnal pruritus ani in children.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enterobiasis is a common infection of school-age children that classically causes nocturnal perianal pruritus because eggs are deposited around the anus at night. Recovery of ovoid eggs from perianal skin collected in the early morning confirms the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida is a recognized infectious cause of pruritus ani but does not produce ovoid eggs on perianal sampling.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Treponema pallidum causes infectious proctitis and is diagnosed by serology, not by perianal egg collection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes infectious proctitis with anorectal pain, tenesmus, and mucopurulent discharge, and is detected by NAAT.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HPV causes condylomata, which can contribute to pruritus ani as visible perianal lesions rather than microscopic eggs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: pinworm (Enterobius vermicularis) infection causes nocturnal perianal itching with eggs recoverable from the perianal skin.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has 4 months of perianal itching. Examination shows mildly excoriated but otherwise normal perianal skin, with no fissure, fistula, mass, or discharge, and no identifiable underlying cause is found. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Frequent cleansing with scented moist wipes after each bowel movement

choices.label: B
choices.text: A prolonged course of a potent topical corticosteroid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gentle cleansing with water, drying, and a barrier ointment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral antibiotics for presumed bacterial infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical excision of the perianal skin

explanation.summary: This item tests initial management of idiopathic pruritus ani, which is aimed at breaking the itch-scratch cycle.
explanation.whyCorrect: When no cause is identified, pruritus ani is classified as idiopathic and treatment focuses on breaking the itch-scratch cycle: gentle cleansing with water only, keeping the area dry, applying a barrier ointment, and avoiding dietary triggers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Wipes and soaps are common causes of contact dermatitis of the perianal skin and should be avoided; cleansing should use water only.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Only a short course of a low-potency topical corticosteroid (1% hydrocortisone for up to 2 weeks) is used, not prolonged potent steroid therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: water-only cleansing, moisture control, and a barrier ointment are the cornerstone of treatment for idiopathic pruritus ani.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral antibiotics have no role; no bacterial infection has been identified, and antibiotics do not address the itch-scratch cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgical excision of perianal skin is not a treatment for pruritus ani; surgery in this region is directed at abscesses, fistulas, fissures, or hemorrhoids.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman with idiopathic pruritus ani has begun cleansing with water only and keeping the perianal skin dry. Her physician also wants to add a topical agent that protects the skin from moisture and irritation. Which of the following is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Zinc oxide ointment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Topical nitroglycerin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Topical nifedipine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mesalamine suppository

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical anesthetic wipes

explanation.summary: This item tests selection of a barrier ointment in the management of pruritus ani.
explanation.whyCorrect: Barrier protection is a core element of pruritus ani management, and the recommended agents are zinc oxide or petroleum jelly. These protect the perianal skin from moisture and irritants while the itch-scratch cycle is broken.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: zinc oxide is a recommended barrier ointment for protecting perianal skin in pruritus ani.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Topical nitroglycerin relaxes internal sphincter spasm in anal fissures and is not a skin barrier.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Topical calcium channel blockers such as nifedipine also target internal sphincter spasm in anal fissures rather than perianal skin protection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesalamine suppositories treat inflammation of the rectal mucosa in ulcerative proctitis, not perianal skin irritation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Wipes, including medicated ones, are a frequent cause of perianal contact dermatitis and should be avoided.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man with pruritus ani has inflamed, excoriated perianal skin despite starting water-only cleansing and a barrier ointment. His physician decides to add a topical corticosteroid to reduce the acute inflammation. Which of the following regimens is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oral prednisone taper over 6 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: 1% hydrocortisone applied for up to 2 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: A potent topical corticosteroid applied daily for 6 months

choices.label: D
choices.text: 1% hydrocortisone applied indefinitely as maintenance

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intralesional corticosteroid injection into the perianal skin

explanation.summary: This item tests the appropriate potency and duration of topical corticosteroid therapy in pruritus ani.
explanation.whyCorrect: A short course of a low-potency topical corticosteroid, specifically 1% hydrocortisone for no more than 2 weeks, can reduce acute inflammation as part of breaking the itch-scratch cycle. It supplements, but does not replace, gentle hygiene, moisture control, and barrier protection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Systemic corticosteroids are not part of the management of pruritus ani, which is a localized skin problem.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: a short course of low-potency 1% hydrocortisone for up to 2 weeks is the recommended steroid regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prolonged potent topical steroid therapy is not recommended; the steroid course is intentionally short and low-potency.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Indefinite steroid maintenance is not appropriate; the course should be limited to about 2 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Injected corticosteroid is not used for pruritus ani; topical low-potency therapy is the recommended approach.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman with several months of perianal itching has a normal anorectal examination. As part of her counseling, her physician recommends eliminating dietary items known to aggravate this condition. Which of the following dietary factors is most appropriate to eliminate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dietary fiber supplements such as psyllium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lactose-containing dairy products

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gluten-containing grains

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coffee, chocolate, and citrus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dietary sodium

explanation.summary: This item tests recognition of the dietary irritants associated with pruritus ani.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dietary irritants are a recognized associated factor in pruritus ani, and the implicated items are coffee, alcohol, chocolate, spicy foods, and citrus. Avoiding these dietary triggers is part of the standard treatment plan.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fiber is used to soften stool and reduce straining in anorectal disease and is not an identified trigger of perianal itching.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lactose is not among the dietary irritants linked to pruritus ani.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gluten is not among the dietary irritants linked to pruritus ani.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: coffee, alcohol, chocolate, spicy foods, and citrus are the dietary irritants associated with pruritus ani.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium restriction has no established role in the management of perianal itching.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman reports 2 months of perianal itching. She cleanses the area with scented moist wipes several times a day and applies an over-the-counter medicated ointment. Examination shows erythematous, irritated perianal skin without fissure, fistula, mass, or discharge. Which of the following is the most likely contributing factor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pinworm infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fecal soilage from a chronic anorectal fistula

choices.label: C
choices.text: Contact dermatitis from topical products

choices.label: D
choices.text: Invasive anal squamous cell carcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ulcerative proctitis

explanation.summary: This item tests recognition of contact dermatitis as a dermatologic cause of pruritus ani.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dermatologic conditions associated with pruritus ani include contact dermatitis, which often arises from wipes, soaps, or topical medications. This patient's daily use of scented wipes and an over-the-counter ointment with erythematous, irritated skin fits this pattern, and treatment includes gentle cleansing with water only.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pinworm infection classically causes nocturnal perianal pruritus in school-age children, and there is no such history or egg identification here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fecal soilage causing itching requires a source such as hemorrhoids, a fissure, a fistula, or incomplete hygiene; no fistula or drainage is present.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: wipes, soaps, and topical medications are common causes of perianal contact dermatitis in pruritus ani.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neoplasia must be excluded in persistent or refractory cases, but this patient has no mass or ulcerated lesion and has a clear irritant exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ulcerative proctitis produces rectal bleeding, urgency, and tenesmus, not isolated perianal skin irritation.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man has had perianal itching for 8 months despite water-only cleansing, moisture control, barrier ointment, and avoidance of dietary triggers. Examination now shows a firm, ulcerated perianal lesion that has not resolved. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin a 6-month course of topical hydrocortisone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perform a Scotch tape test in the early morning

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prescribe topical nifedipine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassure the patient that this represents idiopathic pruritus ani

choices.label: E
choices.text: Biopsy the lesion

explanation.summary: This item tests exclusion of neoplasia in persistent or refractory pruritus ani with an abnormal perianal lesion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neoplasia must be excluded as a cause of pruritus ani, particularly in persistent or refractory cases. Any external anal lesion that is hard, fixed, ulcerated, or fails to resolve should be biopsied to rule out malignancy or referred to a surgeon for diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Topical corticosteroid for pruritus ani is limited to a short low-potency course, and continuing medical therapy would delay diagnosis of a possible malignancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The tape test detects pinworm eggs, which classically cause nocturnal itching in children and would not explain a firm, ulcerated lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Topical calcium channel blockers treat internal sphincter spasm in anal fissures and would not address a persistent perianal mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Idiopathic pruritus ani is diagnosed only when no cause is identified; a firm, ulcerated, non-resolving lesion demands tissue diagnosis first.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: a hard, ulcerated, non-resolving perianal lesion must be biopsied to exclude malignancy.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman has 2 months of rectal bleeding, fecal urgency, and tenesmus. She reports no sexual risk factors, and testing for gonorrhea, chlamydia, herpes simplex virus, and syphilis is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to establish the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Scotch tape test

choices.label: B
choices.text: Colonoscopy with biopsy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Examination under anesthesia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perianal skin biopsy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat nucleic acid amplification testing

explanation.summary: This item tests the diagnostic modality for ulcerative proctitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rectal bleeding, urgency, and tenesmus with negative infectious testing point to ulcerative proctitis, the form of ulcerative colitis limited to the rectum. Diagnosis is made by colonoscopy with biopsy, which also demonstrates normal mucosa proximal to the inflamed rectum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The tape test detects pinworm eggs in patients with perianal itching and would not evaluate rectal inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: ulcerative proctitis is diagnosed by colonoscopy with biopsy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Examination under anesthesia is used when a deep perianal abscess is suspected without external findings.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Perianal skin biopsy evaluates a persistent perianal lesion; this patient's symptoms localize to the rectal mucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Infectious testing has already been performed and was negative; repeating it will not establish the diagnosis.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man presents with anorectal pain, tenesmus, and rectal discharge. His physician is deciding whether the proctitis is infectious or inflammatory in origin. Which of the following historical features would most increase the likelihood of an infectious cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Receptive anal intercourse

choices.label: B
choices.text: A low-fiber diet with chronic straining

choices.label: C
choices.text: A family history of colorectal cancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolonged sitting on the commode

choices.label: E
choices.text: Passage of a large, hard stool one week earlier

explanation.summary: This item tests the risk factor that distinguishes infectious proctitis from inflammatory (ulcerative) proctitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infectious proctitis occurs predominantly in patients who practice receptive anal intercourse, with common pathogens including Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, herpes simplex virus, and Treponema pallidum. This exposure history is what shifts a proctitis presentation toward an infectious rather than inflammatory cause.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: receptive anal intercourse is the characteristic risk factor for infectious proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Low-fiber diet and straining increase venous pressure and predispose to hemorrhoidal disease, not to infectious proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A family history of colorectal cancer is an indication for colonoscopy but does not point toward an infectious cause of proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolonged time on the commode contributes to hemorrhoidal disease and is addressed by limiting toilet time to 5 minutes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Passage of a hard stool causes the initial tear of an anal fissure rather than infection of the rectal mucosa.

questions.stem: A researcher studies topical capsaicin, the pungent compound of chili peppers, as a treatment for pruritus ani. Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which repeated application relieves itching?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It forms an occlusive barrier that protects the skin from moisture and friction

choices.label: B
choices.text: It reduces resting internal anal sphincter tone

choices.label: C
choices.text: It suppresses mucosal inflammation of the rectum

choices.label: D
choices.text: It desensitizes cutaneous nerve endings to pruritic stimuli

choices.label: E
choices.text: It eradicates perianal fungal colonization

explanation.summary: This item tests the mechanism of topical capsaicin in pruritus ani.
explanation.whyCorrect: Capsaicin-sensitive receptors have been identified on nerve fibers involved in itch transmission. Repeated stimulation of these receptors by topical capsaicin desensitizes the nerve endings, making them less responsive to pruritic stimuli such as histamine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Barrier protection is provided by zinc oxide or petroleum jelly, not by capsaicin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reducing internal sphincter tone is the action of topical nitroglycerin or calcium channel blockers used for anal fissures.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Suppressing rectal mucosal inflammation describes topical mesalamine in ulcerative proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: repeated capsaicin stimulation desensitizes itch-transmitting nerve endings so they respond less to pruritic stimuli such as histamine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Capsaicin is not an antifungal agent, and its benefit is not attributed to eradicating candida.

questions.stem: A medical student is asked to define proctitis while presenting a patient with rectal pain, urgency, and tenesmus. Which of the following best describes the underlying pathologic process?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A tear in the anoderm below the dentate line

choices.label: B
choices.text: A tract connecting the anal canal to the perianal skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inflammation of the rectal mucosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Engorgement and prolapse of the anal vascular cushions

choices.label: E
choices.text: Infection of an obstructed anal gland spreading into adjacent spaces

explanation.summary: This item tests the definition of proctitis and its distinction from other benign anorectal diseases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Proctitis is inflammation of the rectal mucosa, classified into two major categories, infectious and inflammatory. It presents with rectal pain, urgency, tenesmus, and bleeding, which matches this patient's symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A tear in the anoderm defines an anal fissure, which causes sharp pain during defecation with a small amount of bright red blood.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A tract from the anal canal to the perianal skin defines an anal fistula, which presents with persistent or recurrent perianal drainage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: proctitis is inflammation of the rectal mucosa, either infectious or inflammatory.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Engorgement and prolapse of the anal vascular cushions describes hemorrhoidal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Infection of an obstructed anal gland describes the cryptoglandular origin of perianal abscess and fistula.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man has 6 weeks of rectal bleeding, urgency, and tenesmus. He denies sexual risk factors and has no rectal discharge. Colonoscopy shows erythematous, granular, friable mucosa with scattered exudate confined to the rectum, with normal-appearing mucosa more proximally. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infectious proctitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ulcerative proctitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Internal hemorrhoidal disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chronic anal fissure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Anal squamous cell carcinoma

explanation.summary: This item tests recognition of ulcerative proctitis from its symptoms and endoscopic pattern.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ulcerative proctitis is ulcerative colitis limited to the rectum and presents with rectal bleeding, urgency, and tenesmus. Endoscopy shows inflamed, friable, granular rectal mucosa with normal colonic mucosa more proximally, which is exactly what was found here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Infectious proctitis occurs predominantly with receptive anal intercourse and typically produces anorectal pain with mucopurulent or bloody discharge; neither is present.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: rectal-limited inflammation with normal proximal mucosa in a patient with bleeding, urgency, and tenesmus is ulcerative proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Internal hemorrhoids cause painless bright red bleeding separate from stool, with prolapse in more advanced disease, not diffuse rectal mucosal inflammation with tenesmus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A chronic anal fissure causes sharp pain with defecation and shows a midline anoderm ulcer with a sentinel tag, not friable rectal mucosa on colonoscopy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anal squamous cell carcinoma presents as a firm, fixed, or ulcerated anal or perianal mass requiring biopsy, not as diffusely inflamed rectal mucosa.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man with receptive anal intercourse has anorectal pain, tenesmus, and mucopurulent rectal discharge. Which of the following organisms is a recognized cause of his condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterobius vermicularis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Helicobacter pylori

choices.label: C
choices.text: Giardia lamblia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Clostridioides difficile

explanation.summary: This item tests the recognized pathogens of infectious proctitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infectious proctitis occurs predominantly in patients with receptive anal intercourse, and common pathogens are Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, herpes simplex virus, and Treponema pallidum. Chlamydia trachomatis is therefore a recognized cause of this presentation, and NAAT is part of the evaluation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterobius vermicularis causes perianal pruritus from nocturnal egg deposition, not proctitis with mucopurulent discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Helicobacter pylori is not among the recognized pathogens of infectious proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Giardia lamblia is not among the pathogens listed as causes of infectious proctitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: Chlamydia trachomatis is a common cause of infectious proctitis and is detected by nucleic acid amplification testing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clostridioides difficile is not among the recognized pathogens of infectious proctitis in this setting.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man reports perianal itching for several months. He also has prolapsing internal hemorrhoids and describes frequent staining of his underwear with stool and moisture, and he has difficulty cleaning the area thoroughly. The perianal skin is moist and excoriated. Which of the following associated factors best explains his itching?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dietary irritant exposure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Psoriasis of the perianal skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pinworm infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Condylomata from human papillomavirus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fecal soilage and perianal moisture

explanation.summary: This item tests recognition of fecal soilage and moisture as a common associated factor in pruritus ani.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fecal soilage and moisture, arising from hemorrhoids, fissures, fistulas, or incomplete hygiene, is a recognized associated factor in pruritus ani. This patient has prolapsing internal hemorrhoids, visible soilage, and moist excoriated skin, and management includes keeping the area dry with barrier protection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dietary irritants such as coffee, alcohol, chocolate, spicy foods, and citrus can contribute, but none is described here while an obvious source of soilage is.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Psoriasis is a dermatologic cause of pruritus ani, but no psoriatic skin findings are described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pinworm infection classically causes nocturnal perianal itching in school-age children and is not suggested by this history.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Condylomata are visible HPV-related perianal lesions, and none is described on examination.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: hemorrhoids with fecal soilage and persistent perianal moisture is a classic associated factor in pruritus ani.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman undergoes a screening colonoscopy. The endoscopist notes that, unlike the small intestine, the outer longitudinal smooth muscle of this organ is not a continuous sheet but is instead condensed into three narrow bands that run along its length. Which of the following is the most likely functional consequence of this muscular arrangement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The wall is gathered into fixed, permanent sacculations that remain in the same location regardless of muscle activity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tonic contraction of the bands, which are shorter than the organ, gathers the wall into haustra

choices.label: C
choices.text: The inner circular muscle layer is absent, so segmental contractions cannot be generated

choices.label: D
choices.text: Luminal contents are advanced only by continuous peristaltic waves traveling the entire length, without any segmental mixing

choices.label: E
choices.text: The bands form two mucosal lips that act as a sphincter regulating entry of chyme

explanation.summary: This item tests the taeniae coli and how their condensation of the outer longitudinal layer creates haustra.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the colon the outer longitudinal muscle is discontinuous and condenses into three bands, the taeniae coli. Because these bands are shorter than the colon itself, their tonic contraction puckers the wall into outward bulges called haustra, which compartmentalize contents and support segmental mixing and slow propulsion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Haustra are not permanent structures; they shift as the circular muscle contracts and relaxes in different segments.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: the three shorter longitudinal bands tonically contract, gathering the wall into haustral sacculations.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The inner circular layer is present throughout the colon and is precisely what contracts to produce haustral churning.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The taeniae coli arrangement supports segmentation and mass movement rather than eliminating segmental mixing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Two lips of mucosa reinforced by thickened circular muscle describe the ileocecal valve, not the taeniae coli.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man undergoes a contrast enema for evaluation of altered bowel habits. Images obtained at the beginning of the study show a series of rounded outward bulges along the wall of the transverse colon. Films repeated several minutes later show bulges of similar appearance, but in different positions along the same segment. Which of the following best explains this observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The bulges are permanent anatomic compartments that were displaced by a change in patient positioning

choices.label: B
choices.text: The three longitudinal muscle bands have lost their tonic contraction entirely

choices.label: C
choices.text: The bulges are produced by the high-amplitude propulsive contractions that occur one to three times per day

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bulges are haustra, which are not fixed and shift as the circular muscle contracts and relaxes

choices.label: E
choices.text: The bulges reflect cecal distension produced by closure of the valve at the ileocolic junction

explanation.summary: This item tests the dynamic, non-permanent nature of haustra.
explanation.whyCorrect: Haustra are the sacculations produced by the puckering effect of the taeniae coli and are a hallmark of normal colonic anatomy, visible both radiographically and endoscopically. They are not permanent structures: they shift position as the circular muscle contracts and relaxes in different segments, which is exactly what serial films show.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Haustra are not fixed anatomic compartments, so no explanation involving displacement of permanent structures is needed.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Loss of taeniae coli tone would abolish the puckering that creates haustra rather than move them; the bulges are still present.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mass movements are infrequent propulsive events that sweep contents over long distances; they do not create the sacculated appearance of the wall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: haustra shift with circular muscle activity, so their location changes between images.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The findings are in the transverse colon wall and reflect haustral anatomy, not cecal distension from ileocecal valve closure.

questions.stem: A physiologist records motility in an isolated segment of human colon. Localized contractions of the circular muscle repeatedly churn contents back and forth within individual sacculations of the wall, mixing them thoroughly while advancing them only slowly along the segment. Which of the following functions is most directly served by this pattern of activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maximizing contact of luminal contents with the absorptive epithelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rapidly advancing fecal material across one-third to one-half of the colon toward the rectum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preventing retrograde movement of bacteria-laden colonic contents into the terminal ileum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Generating the sensation of urgency that precedes defecation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Maintaining resting closure of the anal canal

explanation.summary: This item tests the function of haustral contractions in colonic absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Haustral contractions churn luminal contents within the sacculations formed by the taeniae coli. This mixing maximizes contact between the contents and the absorptive epithelium, facilitating extraction of water and electrolytes as liquid chyme is slowly converted to formed stool over a transit time of 24 to 72 hours.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: haustral churning maximizes mucosal contact for water and electrolyte absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sweeping contents across one-third to one-half of the colon describes mass movements, which contract long segments rather than mixing within a sacculation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Preventing retrograde flow into the ileum is the function of the tonically contracted ileocecal valve.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Urgency preceding defecation is produced by the high-amplitude contractions of mass movements, not by localized mixing contractions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Resting closure of the anal canal is maintained largely by tonic contraction of the internal anal sphincter.

questions.stem: A healthy 30-year-old man eats a normal diet and passes one formed stool each day. Each day approximately 1 to 2 liters of liquid chyme enter his colon from the ileum. Approximately how much water is contained in the stool he passes daily?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 10 to 20 mL

choices.label: B
choices.text: 100 to 200 mL

choices.label: C
choices.text: 500 to 600 mL

choices.label: D
choices.text: 1 to 2 L

choices.label: E
choices.text: 3 to 4 L

explanation.summary: This item tests the quantitative efficiency of colonic water absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 1 to 2 liters of liquid chyme enter the colon from the ileum each day. Highly efficient epithelial transport reclaims the great majority of this fluid, so that only roughly 100 to 200 mL of water remains in the stool that is excreted.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This underestimates normal stool water; formed stool is still about three-fourths water.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: normal daily stool contains approximately 100 to 200 mL of water.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Losses of this magnitude would represent a substantial failure of colonic absorption rather than normal physiology.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This is the volume delivered to the colon each day, not the volume excreted.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This exceeds the volume of chyme the ileum delivers to the colon daily.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with chronic loose stools is counseled about how the colon normally reclaims most of the fluid it receives from the small intestine. Which of the following processes is the primary driver of water reabsorption across the colonic epithelium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Secretion of bicarbonate into the lumen by anion exchangers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sodium absorption through apical sodium channels and Na+/H+ exchangers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Active pumping of water across the apical membrane by an ATP-dependent water pump

choices.label: D
choices.text: Secretion of chloride into the lumen through cyclic AMP-activated apical channels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Secretion of potassium into the lumen down its concentration gradient

explanation.summary: This item tests sodium absorption as the primary driver of colonic water reabsorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sodium absorption is the primary driver of water reabsorption in the colon. Sodium enters colonocytes apically through epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) and Na+/H+ exchangers (NHE) and is then pumped out basolaterally, creating the osmotic gradient that draws water out of the lumen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Apical Cl−/HCO3− exchange absorbs chloride and secretes bicarbonate, explaining alkaline colonic secretions; it is not the main driver of water absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: sodium absorption via ENaC and NHE generates the osmotic force for water uptake.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Water is not actively pumped; it follows osmotically, moving paracellularly into the submucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chloride secretion moves water into the lumen and, when excessive, causes secretory diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The colon both absorbs and secretes potassium depending on luminal and hormonal conditions, but potassium secretion does not drive net water absorption.

questions.stem: Colonocytes from a healthy volunteer are studied in a chamber that allows separate access to the apical and basolateral surfaces. Blocking one basolateral transporter abolishes the transepithelial osmotic gradient and stops net water movement, even though apical sodium entry pathways remain intact. Which of the following best describes the function of the blocked transporter?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It exchanges chloride for bicarbonate at the apical membrane, alkalinizing luminal contents

choices.label: B
choices.text: It permits sodium to enter the cell from the lumen down its electrochemical gradient

choices.label: C
choices.text: It secretes chloride into the lumen when intracellular cyclic AMP rises after toxin exposure

choices.label: D
choices.text: It carries short-chain fatty acids produced by bacterial fermentation into the cell

choices.label: E
choices.text: It actively extrudes sodium from the cell into the submucosa, driving water absorption

explanation.summary: This item tests the role of the basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase in colonic water absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sodium that enters colonocytes apically is actively pumped out across the basolateral membrane by Na+/K+-ATPase. This extrusion creates the osmotic gradient that draws water paracellularly into the submucosa, so blocking it abolishes net water absorption even when apical sodium entry is preserved.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The Cl−/HCO3− exchanger is an apical transporter and explains alkaline colonic secretions rather than the osmotic gradient.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Apical entry through ENaC and NHE is explicitly stated to be intact in this experiment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: cAMP-activated chloride secretion is an apical process that moves fluid into the lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Short-chain fatty acids stimulate sodium and water absorption, but their uptake is not the basolateral pump that generates the gradient.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: the basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase drives sodium out of the cell and establishes the osmotic gradient for water absorption.

questions.stem: Fluid aspirated from the colonic lumen of a healthy adult during endoscopy is alkaline and contains a high concentration of bicarbonate. Which of the following transport processes is most directly responsible for this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sodium entry through apical epithelial sodium channels down its electrochemical gradient

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sodium extrusion by the basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stimulation of sodium absorption by bacterially produced short-chain fatty acids

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apical Cl−/HCO3− exchange, which secretes bicarbonate into the lumen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aldosterone-mediated increases in sodium and water absorption

explanation.summary: This item tests the origin of the alkaline character of colonic secretions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chloride absorption in the colon occurs through apical Cl−/HCO3− exchangers. As chloride is taken up, bicarbonate is simultaneously secreted into the lumen, which explains why colonic secretions are alkaline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ENaC mediates sodium uptake and does not move bicarbonate into the lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase generates the osmotic gradient for water absorption but does not secrete bicarbonate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Short-chain fatty acids promote sodium and water absorption rather than luminal alkalinization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: apical Cl−/HCO3− exchange secretes bicarbonate as chloride is absorbed, alkalinizing colonic contents.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aldosterone increases sodium and water absorption and is not the source of luminal bicarbonate.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man substantially increases the amount of dietary fiber in his diet. Colonic bacteria ferment the additional fiber, and the products of that fermentation act on the colonic epithelium. Which of the following effects is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased secretion of chloride into the colonic lumen through apical CFTR channels

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased activity of the basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased sodium and water absorption by the colonic mucosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of tonic contraction of the ileocecal valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: An increase in mass movements to more than ten episodes per day

explanation.summary: This item tests the effect of short-chain fatty acids on colonic sodium and water absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial fermentation of dietary fiber generates short-chain fatty acids. These stimulate sodium and water absorption by the colonic epithelium, which is the link between the gut microbiome and colonic fluid balance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Increased luminal chloride secretion is the mechanism of secretory diarrhea, not the effect of fermentation products.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Short-chain fatty acids enhance rather than impair sodium absorption, which depends on the basolateral pump.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: short-chain fatty acids stimulate colonic sodium and water absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ileocecal valve tone is governed by ileal and cecal pressure, not by fermentation products.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mass movements normally occur only one to three times per day and are triggered by gastric or duodenal distension after a meal.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with several days of poor oral intake and volume depletion is found to have markedly elevated circulating aldosterone. Which of the following changes in colonic function is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased absorption of sodium and water from the colonic lumen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased secretion of chloride into the colonic lumen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreased activity of apical sodium channels in colonocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of bicarbonate secretion by the colonic epithelium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced production of short-chain fatty acids by colonic bacteria

explanation.summary: This item tests aldosterone as a hormonal control point for colonic sodium and water absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aldosterone acts on the colonic epithelium to increase sodium absorption, and water follows the resulting osmotic gradient. It is therefore a key hormonal control point for colonic fluid balance, and high levels favor greater sodium and water recovery from the lumen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: aldosterone increases colonic sodium and, secondarily, water absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloride secretion into the lumen is driven by cyclic AMP-activated channels, not by aldosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aldosterone promotes rather than suppresses apical sodium entry.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bicarbonate secretion is coupled to apical chloride absorption and is not abolished by aldosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Short-chain fatty acid production depends on bacterial fermentation of dietary fiber, not on mineralocorticoid levels.

questions.stem: A stool specimen from a healthy adult is analyzed in the laboratory. Water accounts for approximately three-fourths of its mass. Which of the following best describes the composition of the remaining solid material?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Predominantly undigested dietary protein and triglyceride that escaped small intestinal absorption

choices.label: B
choices.text: Predominantly precipitated calcium and magnesium salts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Predominantly colonic secretions rich in bicarbonate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Predominantly ingested fluid that was never absorbed by the small intestine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bacteria, undigested fiber, desquamated epithelial cells, and bile pigments

explanation.summary: This item tests the composition of formed stool.
explanation.whyCorrect: By the time colonic contents reach the sigmoid colon and rectum, progressive water and electrolyte absorption has produced formed stool that is roughly 75% water. The remainder consists of bacteria, undigested fiber, desquamated epithelial cells, and bile pigments.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nutrient digestion and absorption occur in the small intestine, so protein and fat are not the major solid residue of normal stool.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mineral salts are not the predominant solid component of normal formed stool.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bicarbonate-rich colonic secretions contribute to the alkalinity of luminal fluid but are not the solid residue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Unabsorbed fluid is water, which is already accounted for by the 75% water content.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: bacteria, undigested fiber, shed epithelial cells, and bile pigments make up the solid fraction of stool.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man develops profuse watery diarrhea after drinking contaminated water while traveling. Stool analysis shows a low osmotic gap. The responsible toxin raises intracellular cyclic AMP in intestinal epithelial cells. Which of the following mechanisms best explains his increased stool water content?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased sodium entry through apical epithelial sodium channels in the distal colon

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excessive chloride secretion through cyclic AMP-activated CFTR channels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excessive aldosterone stimulation of colonic sodium transport

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased production of short-chain fatty acids by fermenting colonic bacteria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prolonged colonic transit with excessive extraction of water

explanation.summary: This item tests the mechanism of secretory diarrhea.
explanation.whyCorrect: In secretory diarrhea, excessive chloride secretion into the lumen through cyclic AMP-activated CFTR channels, as occurs in cholera, overwhelms the absorptive capacity of the intestine and produces watery stools with a low osmotic gap.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Increased sodium absorption through ENaC would promote water reabsorption and firmer stool.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: cAMP-driven chloride secretion exceeding absorptive capacity is the mechanism of secretory diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aldosterone increases sodium and water absorption and would oppose, not cause, watery stools.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Short-chain fatty acids stimulate sodium and water absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolonged transit causes hard, dry stools, the opposite of this presentation.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man reports hard, dry, pellet-like stools that are difficult to pass and bowel movements only twice a week. A marker study shows markedly prolonged colonic transit. Which of the following best explains the consistency of his stool?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chloride secretion into the lumen exceeds sodium absorption

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bicarbonate secretion by the colonic epithelium is reduced

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prolonged colonic transit permits excessive extraction of water

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rapid delivery of chyme through the ileocecal valve overwhelms colonic absorption

choices.label: E
choices.text: The internal anal sphincter fails to relax in response to rectal distension

explanation.summary: This item tests why slow colonic transit produces hard stool.
explanation.whyCorrect: Colonic water absorption is time-dependent. When transit is prolonged, as in slow-transit constipation, luminal contents remain in contact with the absorptive epithelium longer, allowing excessive water extraction and producing hard, dry stools that are difficult to pass.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Excess chloride secretion produces watery stools, not hard ones.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reduced bicarbonate secretion would alter luminal pH rather than stool consistency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: prolonged transit allows excessive water extraction, producing hard, dry stool.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rapid delivery of chyme into the colon overwhelms absorption and causes loose stools.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Failure of the internal anal sphincter to relax with rectal distension describes an absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex, which is not indicated in this vignette and would not by itself explain stool water content.

questions.stem: During an abdominal operation, a surgeon inspects the junction of the terminal ileum and the cecum. The structure there consists of two lips of mucosa reinforced by thickened circular smooth muscle that is tonically contracted at rest, keeping the passage closed. Which of the following is the most important consequence of this resting tone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It prevents reflux of acidic gastric contents into the small intestine

choices.label: B
choices.text: It generates the mass movements that advance stool toward the rectum after meals

choices.label: C
choices.text: It maintains the alkaline pH of colonic secretions

choices.label: D
choices.text: It prevents retrograde flow of colonic contents into the ileum

choices.label: E
choices.text: It provides the majority of resting pressure in the anal canal

explanation.summary: This item tests the barrier function of the tonically closed ileocecal valve.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ileocecal valve is a sphincter-like structure whose thickened circular smooth muscle remains tonically contracted at rest. This keeps the valve closed and prevents retrograde flow of bacteria-laden colonic contents back into the ileum, a critical defense against small intestinal bacterial overgrowth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gastric contents are retained by sphincters at the stomach, not by the ileocecal valve.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mass movements are produced by contraction of long colonic segments mediated by the enteric nervous system.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Alkaline colonic secretions result from apical Cl−/HCO3− exchange in colonocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: tonic closure prevents colonic bacteria from refluxing into the ileum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Most resting anal canal pressure is supplied by tonic contraction of the internal anal sphincter.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman undergoes right hemicolectomy for a cecal mass; the ileocecal valve is removed with the specimen. Several months later she reports frequent loose stools and bloating. Which of the following complications is most directly attributable to loss of this structure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased gastric acid secretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduced bile acid reabsorption

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bacterial overgrowth in the small intestine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decreased gastrin secretion by antral G cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Absence of the rectoanal inhibitory reflex

explanation.summary: This item tests the consequence of losing ileocecal valve function.
explanation.whyCorrect: The tonically closed ileocecal valve normally prevents bacteria-laden colonic contents from refluxing into the ileum. When it is resected, as in right hemicolectomy, that barrier is lost and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, along with diarrhea, can result.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gastric acid secretion is regulated by gastric mechanisms and is not controlled by the ileocecal valve.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bile acid handling is not the function attributed to the ileocecal valve itself.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: loss of the valve permits retrograde bacterial flow and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gastrin release from antral G cells is triggered by a meal and is independent of ileocecal valve integrity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex reflects loss of enteric ganglion cells in the distal colon, not valve resection.

questions.stem: In an anesthetized animal, a balloon placed in the cecum is progressively inflated while pressure is recorded at the ileocecal junction. Which of the following responses is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contraction of the ileocecal valve, slowing further entry of chyme into the colon

choices.label: B
choices.text: Relaxation of the ileocecal valve, allowing more rapid entry of chyme into the colon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Relaxation of the internal anal sphincter

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immediate initiation of a mass movement in the ascending colon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased secretion of gastrin by antral G cells

explanation.summary: This item tests the feedback control of the ileocecal valve by cecal distension.
explanation.whyCorrect: Distension of the cecum triggers contraction of the ileocecal valve, slowing further entry of chyme from the ileum. This feedback mechanism protects the colon from being overwhelmed with luminal contents.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: cecal distension closes the valve more tightly, limiting further filling.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Valve relaxation is produced by ileal peristaltic waves and increased ileal pressure, not by cecal distension.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Internal anal sphincter relaxation follows rectal, not cecal, distension.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mass movements are typically triggered by gastric or duodenal distension after a meal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gastrin release is stimulated by a meal reaching the stomach, not by cecal distension.

questions.stem: Shortly after a large meal reaches the stomach, peristaltic activity in the terminal ileum increases and ileal contents are delivered through the ileocecal valve into the cecum. Both gastric distension and a hormone released by antral G cells contribute to this response. Which of the following best describes its net effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It prevents entry of chyme into the colon until the stomach has emptied completely

choices.label: B
choices.text: It relaxes the internal anal sphincter in preparation for defecation

choices.label: C
choices.text: It reduces the amplitude of haustral contractions so that contents are stored in the colon

choices.label: D
choices.text: It slows ileal peristalsis so that nutrient absorption can be completed

choices.label: E
choices.text: It empties the ileum into the colon, making room for the contents of the incoming meal

explanation.summary: This item tests the gastroileal reflex and its role in colonic filling.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gastroileal reflex is a neurohormonal response in which gastric distension, together with gastrin released by antral G cells, increases ileal peristalsis. This accelerates delivery of ileal contents through the ileocecal valve into the cecum, a coordinated make-room response that promotes colonic filling in anticipation of the incoming meal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The reflex promotes rather than blocks entry of chyme into the colon after a meal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Internal anal sphincter relaxation belongs to the defecation reflex triggered by rectal distension.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Haustral contractions continue to mix and absorb; the reflex does not suppress them to store contents.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The reflex accelerates rather than slows ileal peristalsis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: the ileum empties into the colon as the stomach fills, making room for the new meal.

questions.stem: Colonic manometry in a healthy adult records an event in which a long segment of transverse and descending colon contracts simultaneously while the segment ahead of it relaxes, rapidly advancing contents toward the rectum. This event is captured twice during the 24-hour recording, each time shortly after a meal. Which of the following best characterizes this event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A haustral contraction that mixes contents within a single sacculation of the transverse colon

choices.label: B
choices.text: A mass movement, which sweeps contents across one-third to one-half of the colon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tonic contraction of the taeniae coli that maintains baseline wall tension between meals

choices.label: D
choices.text: The rectoanal inhibitory reflex

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relaxation of the ileocecal valve in response to ileal distension

explanation.summary: This item tests the defining features of mass movements.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mass movements are powerful propulsive contractions characterized by simultaneous contraction of a long colonic segment with relaxation ahead of it, sweeping contents over one-third to one-half of the colon. They occur infrequently, typically one to three times per day, and are most often triggered by gastric or duodenal distension after a meal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Haustral contractions are localized and mixing in nature rather than propulsive over long distances.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: the long-segment simultaneous contraction with distal relaxation, occurring a few times daily after meals, defines a mass movement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Taeniae coli tone is a sustained baseline tension that produces haustra, not a discrete propulsive event.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The rectoanal inhibitory reflex is relaxation of the internal anal sphincter in response to rectal distension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ileocecal valve relaxation governs entry of chyme into the cecum, not propulsion through the transverse and descending colon.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman notes that she reliably feels an urge to move her bowels within about 20 minutes of starting breakfast. This response begins when food distends her stomach and is amplified by gastrin and cholecystokinin. Which of the following changes in colonic function most directly produces her symptom?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tonic contraction of the ileocecal valve in response to cecal distension

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased paracellular absorption of water and electrolytes in the ascending colon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of tone in the taeniae coli with flattening of the haustra

choices.label: D
choices.text: A marked increase in colonic motility with initiation of mass movements

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relaxation of the external anal sphincter via the pudendal nerve

explanation.summary: This item tests the gastrocolic reflex as the cause of postprandial urgency.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gastrocolic reflex is initiated by gastric distension and triggers enteric and extrinsic neural signals, carried by the vagus and pelvic nerves, that dramatically increase colonic motility and initiate mass movements. Gastrin and cholecystokinin amplify this response, and the resulting high-amplitude contractions produce the postprandial urge to defecate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ileocecal valve contraction slows colonic filling and does not generate an urge to defecate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased water absorption changes stool consistency rather than producing urgency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Loss of taeniae coli tone would abolish haustra and is not a postprandial event.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: gastric distension triggers the gastrocolic reflex, increasing colonic motility and initiating mass movements.
whyWrongByChoice.E: External anal sphincter relaxation is a voluntary final step of defecation, not the reflex increase in colonic motility that creates the urge.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man undergoes anorectal manometry. A balloon is inflated in his rectum to simulate the arrival of stool, and resting pressure in the anal canal falls promptly. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rectal stretch receptors trigger reflex relaxation of the internal anal sphincter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Voluntary cortical signals travel in the corticospinal tract to relax the external anal sphincter

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sympathetic fibers from the L1 and L2 segments increase internal anal sphincter tone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Haustral contractions in the sigmoid colon transiently lower anal canal pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gastrin released after a meal relaxes the anal sphincters

explanation.summary: This item tests the rectoanal inhibitory reflex component of the defecation reflex.
explanation.whyCorrect: When fecal material distends the rectum, stretch receptors activate the enteric nervous system and trigger the rectoanal inhibitory reflex, relaxing the internal anal sphincter. Because the internal sphincter supplies most resting anal canal pressure, this intrinsic reflex is recorded as a prompt fall in resting pressure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: rectal distension activates an enteric reflex that relaxes the internal anal sphincter.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cortical control through the corticospinal tract governs voluntary external sphincter activity, which is not what a reflex pressure drop measures.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sympathetic hypogastric input contracts the internal sphincter and would raise, not lower, resting pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Haustral contractions mix colonic contents and do not control anal canal pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gastrin enhances ileal motility and amplifies the gastrocolic reflex; it does not mediate sphincter relaxation on rectal distension.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman feels the urge to defecate during a meeting and successfully defers the bowel movement until she can reach a restroom. Which of the following best describes the structure responsible for this deferral?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Smooth muscle innervated by sympathetic fibers traveling in the hypogastric nerve

choices.label: B
choices.text: Smooth muscle that is a thickened continuation of the inner circular layer of the rectum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skeletal muscle innervated by the pudendal nerve, capable of rapid voluntary contraction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Smooth muscle relaxed by parasympathetic fibers traveling in the pelvic nerve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Three bands of longitudinal smooth muscle that tonically contract along the bowel wall

explanation.summary: This item tests the composition and innervation of the external anal sphincter.
explanation.whyCorrect: The external anal sphincter is skeletal (striated) muscle innervated by the pudendal nerve (S2 to S4), a somatic nerve, with cortical input through the corticospinal tract. It is capable of rapid, forceful voluntary contraction and can be consciously contracted to defer defecation when it is socially inconvenient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sympathetic hypogastric innervation supplies the internal anal sphincter and acts involuntarily.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A thickened continuation of the rectal inner circular smooth muscle describes the internal anal sphincter, which is not under voluntary control.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: the external anal sphincter is skeletal muscle under pudendal, voluntary control.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Parasympathetic pelvic fibers relax the internal anal sphincter and facilitate rather than defer defecation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The taeniae coli are colonic longitudinal muscle bands that create haustra and have no role in continence.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman reports that she feels a strong urge to move her bowels within 15 minutes of eating breakfast nearly every morning. She has no abdominal pain, weight loss, or blood in the stool, and her physical examination is normal. Which of the following best explains her postprandial urge?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Haustral contractions increasing in amplitude to churn colonic contents

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct chemical stimulation of rectal mucosa by nutrients absorbed at breakfast

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gastric distension triggering colonic mass movements

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased ileal peristalsis emptying the terminal ileum into the cecum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sympathetic discharge along the hypogastric nerve increasing internal anal sphincter tone

explanation.summary: This item tests the gastrocolic reflex as the trigger for postprandial mass movements.
explanation.whyCorrect: Food entering the stomach causes gastric distension, which initiates enteric nervous system and extrinsic neural signaling (vagus and pelvic nerves) that markedly increases colonic motility and initiates mass movements. The high-amplitude propulsive contractions of mass movements deliver stool to the rectum and generate the sensation of urgency that precedes defecation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Haustral contractions are localized, mixing contractions that maximize mucosal contact for water and electrolyte absorption; they do not propel stool into the rectum or produce urgency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Urgency after eating is generated by a neurally mediated motility reflex from gastric distension, not by absorbed nutrients acting on rectal mucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: gastric distension after a meal triggers the gastrocolic reflex, which initiates mass movements and the resulting urge to defecate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Accelerated ileal peristalsis promotes colonic filling from the ileum, but the urge to defecate arises from mass movements delivering stool to the rectum, not from chyme entering the cecum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sympathetic input to the internal anal sphincter promotes contraction and continence; it would oppose, not produce, an urge to defecate.

questions.stem: A physiologist records intraluminal pressure in the colon of a healthy adult volunteer over 24 hours and identifies episodes in which a long colonic segment contracts simultaneously and advances contents over one-third of the colon. How often do these high-amplitude propulsive contractions typically occur in a healthy adult?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 10 to 12 times per hour

choices.label: B
choices.text: 1 to 3 times per day

choices.label: C
choices.text: 1 to 3 times per hour

choices.label: D
choices.text: Once every 3 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: 20 to 30 times per day

explanation.summary: This item tests the normal frequency of colonic mass movements.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mass movements are powerful propulsive contractions that sweep contents over long distances, sometimes one-third to one-half of the colon in a single contraction. They occur infrequently, typically 1 to 3 times per day, most often after a meal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This frequency would describe rapid, repetitive activity rather than the infrequent propulsive events that characterize mass movements.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: mass movements occur roughly 1 to 3 times per day, usually triggered by gastric or duodenal distension after a meal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mass movements are far less frequent than once or more per hour; the localized churning of haustral contractions accounts for the ongoing motility between them.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This is too infrequent; normal colonic transit of 24 to 72 hours depends on mass movements occurring at least once daily.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This grossly overestimates their frequency; mass movements are notable precisely because they are infrequent and high-amplitude.

questions.stem: During an operation on the anal canal, a surgeon identifies the innermost sphincteric ring surrounding the anal canal. Which of the following best describes the composition and origin of this structure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Smooth muscle formed by thickening of the inner circular layer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Skeletal muscle formed by condensation of the outer longitudinal layer of the rectal wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smooth muscle derived from the taeniae coli as they converge at the rectum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skeletal muscle that receives its motor supply from the pelvic nerve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smooth muscle arranged as a striated ring outside the external sphincter

explanation.summary: This item tests the muscle composition and origin of the internal anal sphincter.
