explanation.whyCorrect: The internal anal sphincter is the innermost sphincter of the anal canal and is composed of smooth muscle representing a thickened continuation of the inner circular muscle layer of the rectum. Because it is smooth muscle, it operates involuntarily and maintains tonic contraction at rest.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: the internal anal sphincter is smooth muscle continuous with the thickened inner circular layer of the rectum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The outer longitudinal layer of the colon condenses into the taeniae coli; it does not form a skeletal-muscle sphincter at the anal canal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The taeniae coli are longitudinal bands of the colonic wall that create haustra; they are not the source of the internal sphincter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The skeletal-muscle sphincter of the anal canal is the external sphincter, and it is supplied by the somatic pudendal nerve, not the pelvic nerve.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The internal sphincter lies inside the external sphincter, which is the striated ring surrounding it.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man undergoing evaluation for fecal soiling is asked to squeeze as though preventing a bowel movement, and anal canal pressure rises sharply. Which of the following nerves carries the motor fibers responsible for this pressure increase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hypogastric nerve (L1-L2)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pelvic nerve (S2-S4) parasympathetic fibers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vagus nerve

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pudendal nerve (S2-S4)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intrinsic fibers of the myenteric plexus

explanation.summary: This item tests the somatic innervation of the external anal sphincter.
explanation.whyCorrect: A voluntary squeeze raises anal canal pressure by contracting the external anal sphincter, which is skeletal muscle. It is innervated by the pudendal nerve (S2-S4), a somatic nerve, and receives cortical input by way of the corticospinal tract to allow conscious control.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sympathetic hypogastric fibers act on the internal anal sphincter, promoting its tonic contraction; they do not mediate voluntary squeeze.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Parasympathetic pelvic nerve fibers cause internal anal sphincter relaxation and facilitate defecation rather than voluntary sphincter contraction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vagal fibers participate in reflex increases in colonic motility, not in voluntary contraction of the anal sphincter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: the pudendal nerve (S2-S4) supplies the skeletal-muscle external anal sphincter and mediates voluntary squeeze.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The myenteric plexus mediates the intrinsic reflex that relaxes the internal sphincter and is not under voluntary control.

questions.stem: During anorectal manometry, a resting pressure is recorded in the anal canal of a healthy 30-year-old man who is instructed to lie quietly and not squeeze. Which of the following accounts for the majority of the pressure measured under these conditions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Phasic contraction of the external anal sphincter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tonic contraction of the taeniae coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cortically driven firing of the pudendal nerve to striated sphincter muscle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peristaltic contraction of rectal smooth muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tonic contraction of the internal anal sphincter

explanation.summary: This item tests the contribution of the internal anal sphincter to resting anal canal pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The internal anal sphincter maintains a state of tonic contraction at rest and provides roughly 70% to 85% of resting anal canal pressure. This sustained smooth muscle tone underlies passive continence, preventing leakage without conscious effort.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The external sphincter has a resting tone that is lower than that of the internal sphincter and rises substantially only with voluntary effort.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The taeniae coli generate tension along the colon and contribute to haustra and segmental contractions; they do not generate anal canal pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cortical drive through the pudendal nerve produces voluntary squeeze pressure, which is not being generated in a resting, unsqueezing subject.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rectal peristalsis propels contents toward the anal canal and is not the source of resting sphincter pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: tonic contraction of the internal anal sphincter supplies about 70% to 85% of resting anal canal pressure.

questions.stem: A 3-week-old infant is evaluated for delayed passage of meconium, abdominal distension, and difficulty stooling since birth. Anorectal manometry shows that inflation of a rectal balloon fails to produce any fall in anal canal resting pressure. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hirschsprung disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pudendal nerve injury sustained during delivery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Slow-transit constipation from reduced mass movements

choices.label: D
choices.text: Internal anal sphincter degeneration causing passive incontinence

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fecal impaction of the rectosigmoid

explanation.summary: This item tests recognition of an absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex as the hallmark of Hirschsprung disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hirschsprung disease results from congenital absence of enteric ganglion cells in a segment of distal colon, most commonly the rectosigmoid. Because the intrinsic reflex arc is missing, the internal anal sphincter fails to relax when the rectum is distended, and an absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex on anorectal manometry is the hallmark diagnostic finding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: absence of enteric ganglion cells eliminates the intrinsic reflex arc, so the rectoanal inhibitory reflex is absent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pudendal nerve injury impairs voluntary external sphincter contraction and produces incontinence, not an absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reduced mass movements prolong transit and produce hard stools but do not abolish the intrinsic reflex that relaxes the internal sphincter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Loss of internal sphincter tone lowers resting pressure and causes leakage at rest rather than failure of reflex relaxation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Impaction is a consequence of impaired propulsion and would not by itself abolish the reflex relaxation of the internal sphincter.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman reports that since a prolonged forceps-assisted delivery 6 weeks ago she senses when her rectum fills but cannot hold stool long enough to reach a toilet. Anorectal manometry shows normal resting pressure, a markedly reduced squeeze pressure, and a normal fall in anal pressure with rectal balloon distension. Which of the following best explains her incontinence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Injury to hypogastric sympathetic fibers with loss of resting internal anal sphincter tone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of enteric ganglion cells with an absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pudendal nerve injury with absent voluntary external sphincter control

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excess sympathetic input with sustained internal sphincter contraction and high resting pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Failure of sacral parasympathetic fibers to increase rectal peristalsis

explanation.summary: This item tests the pattern of urge incontinence produced by external anal sphincter denervation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pudendal nerve, which supplies the skeletal-muscle external anal sphincter, can be injured during childbirth or pelvic surgery, and such injury produces fecal incontinence from loss of voluntary sphincter control. Her preserved rectal sensation with inability to defer defecation is the classic urge pattern, and manometry confirms normal resting (internal sphincter) pressure with reduced squeeze (external sphincter) pressure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Loss of internal sphincter tone would lower resting pressure and cause passive leakage at rest, but her resting pressure is normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Absence of enteric ganglion cells abolishes the rectoanal inhibitory reflex, yet her anal pressure falls normally with balloon distension.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: pudendal nerve injury from an operative vaginal delivery abolishes voluntary external sphincter contraction, producing urge incontinence with a low squeeze pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased internal sphincter contraction would favor continence and would raise, not lower, measured pressures.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Impaired sacral parasympathetic augmentation of rectal contraction would hinder expulsion rather than cause incontinence.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with long-standing autonomic neuropathy reports that he passes gas and small amounts of liquid stool without being aware of it, often noticing soiling only when he undresses. He denies straining and can squeeze on command when asked. Which of the following best explains his symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inability to voluntarily contract the external anal sphincter on command

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of internal anal sphincter tone with low resting pressure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Absence of the rectoanal inhibitory reflex

choices.label: D
choices.text: An exaggerated gastrocolic reflex producing more frequent postprandial mass movements

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced frequency and amplitude of colonic mass movements

explanation.summary: This item tests recognition of passive incontinence as a manifestation of internal anal sphincter failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Internal anal sphincter dysfunction, such as from smooth muscle degeneration or autonomic neuropathy, causes passive incontinence: involuntary leakage at rest, particularly of liquid stool and gas, because resting anal canal pressure is lost. His preserved voluntary squeeze places the defect in the involuntary rather than the somatic component.

whyWrongByChoice.A: He can squeeze on command, indicating that voluntary external sphincter function is intact.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: loss of internal sphincter tone lowers resting anal canal pressure and produces unnoticed leakage of gas and liquid stool.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex causes failure of sphincter relaxation and obstructed defecation, not resting leakage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An exaggerated gastrocolic reflex would produce postprandial urgency, not passive soiling that the patient does not perceive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reduced mass movements slow transit and produce hard, infrequent stools rather than leakage.

questions.stem: A physiologist studies the sequence of events that culminates in defecation in a healthy adult. Which of the following events initiates the defecation reflex?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Voluntary relaxation of the external anal sphincter during straining

choices.label: B
choices.text: Performance of a sustained Valsalva maneuver

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sympathetic discharge along the hypogastric nerve to the anal canal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Distension of the rectal wall by entering feces

choices.label: E
choices.text: Contraction of the internal anal sphincter

explanation.summary: This item tests the initiating step of the defecation reflex.
explanation.whyCorrect: When mass movements propel fecal material into the rectum, rectal wall distension activates stretch receptors that trigger the reflex. These receptors activate the enteric nervous system, producing the rectoanal inhibitory reflex with internal anal sphincter relaxation, after which sacral parasympathetic signals increase rectal peristalsis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Voluntary external sphincter relaxation is a later, voluntary step that permits defecation once the reflex is under way.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The Valsalva maneuver raises intra-abdominal pressure to facilitate expulsion and occurs at the end of the sequence.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sympathetic hypogastric activity maintains internal sphincter contraction and continence rather than initiating defecation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: fecal matter entering the rectum distends the rectal wall and activates stretch receptors, initiating the reflex.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Internal sphincter contraction maintains continence; the reflex causes its relaxation.

questions.stem: In an anesthetized animal, an investigator electrically stimulates the hypogastric nerve and records pressure in the anal canal. Which of the following effects is most likely to result from this stimulation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Relaxation of the internal anal sphincter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contraction of the external anal sphincter

choices.label: C
choices.text: Relaxation of the external anal sphincter

choices.label: D
choices.text: Abolition of the rectoanal inhibitory reflex

choices.label: E
choices.text: Contraction of the internal anal sphincter

explanation.summary: This item tests the sympathetic control of the internal anal sphincter.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sympathetic fibers arising from L1-L2 travel in the hypogastric nerve and promote contraction of the internal anal sphincter, thereby maintaining continence. Stimulating this pathway therefore raises anal canal pressure through smooth muscle contraction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Relaxation of the internal sphincter is produced by parasympathetic fibers of the pelvic nerve and by the intrinsic reflex, not by sympathetic stimulation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The external sphincter is skeletal muscle driven by the somatic pudendal nerve and is not controlled by the hypogastric nerve.
whyWrongByChoice.C: External sphincter relaxation is a voluntary somatic event mediated through the pudendal nerve.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The rectoanal inhibitory reflex is intrinsic to the enteric nervous system and is not abolished by stimulating a sympathetic nerve.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: sympathetic fibers in the hypogastric nerve contract the internal anal sphincter and support continence.

questions.stem: A medical student is reviewing the autonomic control of the anal canal. Which of the following actions is produced by parasympathetic fibers traveling in the pelvic nerve to the anal canal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Contraction of the internal anal sphincter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Relaxation of the internal anal sphincter

choices.label: C
choices.text: Voluntary contraction of the external anal sphincter

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of colonic mass movements

choices.label: E
choices.text: Somatic contraction of the external anal sphincter

explanation.summary: This item tests the parasympathetic contribution to internal anal sphincter control.
explanation.whyCorrect: Parasympathetic fibers from S2-S4 reach the anal canal through the pelvic nerve and cause relaxation of the internal anal sphincter, facilitating defecation. This is the opposite of the sympathetic hypogastric input, which contracts the sphincter and maintains continence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Contraction of the internal sphincter is the sympathetic action carried by the hypogastric nerve.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: pelvic nerve parasympathetic fibers relax the internal anal sphincter and facilitate defecation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Voluntary external sphincter contraction depends on somatic pudendal fibers under cortical control, not autonomic pelvic fibers.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Parasympathetic activity supports colonic motility and defecation rather than inhibiting mass movements.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The external sphincter is skeletal muscle supplied by the somatic pudendal nerve, not by parasympathetic pelvic fibers.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man feels an urge to defecate during a meeting and successfully postpones defecation until the meeting ends. Which of the following mechanisms allowed him to defer defecation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Voluntary contraction of the skeletal-muscle external anal sphincter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Voluntary contraction of the smooth-muscle internal anal sphincter

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sympathetically mediated relaxation of the external anal sphincter via the hypogastric nerve

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pudendal nerve suppression of the rectoanal inhibitory reflex during filling

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased haustral churning that prevents rectal filling

explanation.summary: This item tests voluntary control of the external anal sphincter in deferring defecation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The external anal sphincter is skeletal muscle innervated by the pudendal nerve and driven by cortical input, so it is capable of rapid, forceful voluntary contraction. This voluntary contraction is what allows defecation to be deferred when it is socially inconvenient, even though the internal sphincter has already relaxed reflexively.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: conscious contraction of the striated external sphincter defers defecation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The internal sphincter is smooth muscle under autonomic and enteric control and cannot be contracted at will.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Relaxation of the external sphincter would permit rather than defer defecation, and this muscle is not under sympathetic control.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The rectoanal inhibitory reflex is an intrinsic enteric reflex and is not suppressed by the somatic pudendal nerve.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Haustral contractions mix contents and aid absorption; they do not block rectal filling or provide voluntary continence.

questions.stem: A researcher compares two motility patterns recorded in the human colon. One pattern is localized and mixes contents within individual sacculations; the other rapidly advances fecal material toward the rectum. Which of the following best describes the second pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Localized ring contractions that churn contents within a single sacculation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tonic tension generated by the taeniae coli along the entire colonic wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Slow retrograde movement of contents back toward the cecum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rhythmic segmentation confined to short adjacent segments of the colon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Simultaneous contraction of a long segment with distal relaxation

explanation.summary: This item tests the contractile pattern that distinguishes mass movements from haustral contractions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mass movements are characterized by simultaneous contraction of a long colonic segment with relaxation ahead of it, rapidly advancing fecal material toward the rectum, sometimes across one-third to one-half of the colon. Haustral contractions, by contrast, are localized and mixing in nature.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This describes haustral contractions, the localized mixing pattern that maximizes mucosal contact for absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tonic taeniae coli tension contributes to segmental contractions and haustral puckering rather than to rapid propulsion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Colonic propulsion during mass movements advances contents toward the rectum, not backward toward the cecum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Segmental activity confined to short adjacent segments mixes contents slowly and does not sweep material over long distances.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: mass movements contract a long segment simultaneously while the region ahead relaxes, propelling stool toward the rectum.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man has had 3 months of constipation with straining and hard, infrequent stools. Examination reveals decreased bowel sounds and a palpable mass in the left lower abdomen. Which of the following mechanisms best accounts for his findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excessive chloride and water secretion into the colonic lumen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of voluntary control of the external anal sphincter during straining

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduced mass movements with slow transit and excess water absorption

choices.label: D
choices.text: An exaggerated gastrocolic reflex producing more frequent mass movements

choices.label: E
choices.text: Impaired colonic sodium absorption limiting water extraction from stool

explanation.summary: This item tests the mechanism of slow-transit constipation and stool accumulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reduced frequency or amplitude of mass movements is a key mechanism of slow-transit constipation, and prolonged colonic transit allows excessive water extraction, producing hard, dry stools that are difficult to pass. Formed stool then accumulates where propulsive motility fails, which fits a palpable left lower quadrant mass, while decreased bowel sounds reflect globally reduced colonic motility.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Excessive chloride secretion overwhelms absorptive capacity and produces watery stools, the opposite of his presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Loss of voluntary external sphincter control causes incontinence, not constipation with a palpable stool mass.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: diminished mass movements prolong transit, allowing excessive water absorption, hard stools, and accumulation of formed stool in the left colon.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An exaggerated gastrocolic reflex would increase propulsion and postprandial urgency rather than cause retention.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Impaired sodium-driven water absorption would leave stool more liquid rather than hard and dry.

questions.stem: During anorectal manometry, a balloon is inflated in the rectum of a healthy adult and resting anal canal pressure abruptly falls. Which of the following reflexes is being demonstrated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gastrocolic reflex

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gastroileal reflex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cortically mediated squeeze reflex

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rectoanal inhibitory reflex

choices.label: E
choices.text: Valsalva-augmented expulsion reflex

explanation.summary: This item tests identification of the rectoanal inhibitory reflex on manometry.
explanation.whyCorrect: The rectoanal inhibitory reflex is relaxation of the internal anal sphincter in response to rectal distension, which is recorded as a fall in anal canal pressure when a rectal balloon is inflated. It is an intrinsic reflex mediated by the enteric nervous system, and its absence is the hallmark of Hirschsprung disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The gastrocolic reflex is triggered by gastric distension and increases colonic motility, including mass movements.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The gastroileal reflex accelerates ileal peristalsis after a meal to promote colonic filling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A voluntary squeeze raises rather than lowers anal canal pressure and depends on somatic pudendal input.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: rectal distension producing internal anal sphincter relaxation is the rectoanal inhibitory reflex.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The Valsalva maneuver is a voluntary increase in intra-abdominal pressure that assists expulsion, not a response to balloon distension.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman reports fecal incontinence and it is unclear whether the internal or the external anal sphincter is at fault. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to distinguish between these two possibilities?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Colonic transit study with ingested radiopaque markers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anorectal manometry of sphincter pressures

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measurement of the stool osmotic gap

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plain abdominal radiography of the pelvis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Measurement of serum aldosterone and cortisol

explanation.summary: This item tests the use of anorectal manometry to localize sphincter dysfunction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Anorectal manometry distinguishes internal from external sphincter failure by measuring resting pressure, which reflects internal anal sphincter tone, and squeeze pressure, which reflects voluntary external anal sphincter contraction. A low resting pressure points to the internal sphincter, whereas a low squeeze pressure points to the external sphincter.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A transit study assesses how quickly contents move through the colon and does not evaluate sphincter function.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correct: manometry separates internal sphincter (resting pressure) from external sphincter (squeeze pressure) dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The stool osmotic gap is used in evaluating diarrhea mechanisms and says nothing about sphincter competence.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plain radiography can show retained stool but cannot measure sphincter pressures.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aldosterone influences colonic sodium and water absorption, not anal sphincter function.

questions.stem: A healthy adult sits on the toilet after feeling an urge to defecate. Rectal distension has already produced internal anal sphincter relaxation and rectal peristalsis, and he then voluntarily relaxes his external anal sphincter. Which of the following most directly facilitates expulsion of stool at this point?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rectoanal inhibitory reflex relaxation of the internal anal sphincter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sympathetic discharge along the hypogastric nerve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Haustral churning of contents in the transverse colon

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opening of the ileocecal valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: A Valsalva maneuver that raises intra-abdominal pressure

explanation.summary: This item tests the final, voluntary step of the defecation sequence.
explanation.whyCorrect: After voluntary relaxation of the external anal sphincter permits defecation, the Valsalva maneuver increases intra-abdominal pressure and facilitates expulsion. This is the last step in the sequence that begins with rectal distension.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Internal sphincter relaxation has already occurred earlier in the sequence and is not the step that follows external sphincter relaxation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sympathetic hypogastric activity contracts the internal sphincter and supports continence rather than expulsion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Haustral churning mixes contents and aids absorption far upstream from the rectum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Opening of the ileocecal valve regulates delivery of chyme into the cecum and has no role in expelling stool from the rectum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Correct: the Valsalva maneuver raises intra-abdominal pressure and facilitates expulsion after voluntary external sphincter relaxation.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with irritable bowel syndrome describes cramping and an urgent need to defecate soon after meals. The increase in colonic motility she experiences is initiated by gastric distension and amplified by circulating hormones. Which of the following pairs of hormones amplifies this response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aldosterone and secretin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Secretin and somatostatin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gastrin and cholecystokinin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cholecystokinin and aldosterone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Somatostatin and gastrin

explanation.summary: This item tests the hormonal amplification of the gastrocolic reflex.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gastrocolic reflex begins with gastric distension and is carried by enteric and extrinsic neural signals through the vagus and pelvic nerves, dramatically increasing colonic motility and initiating mass movements. Gastrin and cholecystokinin amplify this response, which is exaggerated in conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aldosterone acts on colonic sodium and water absorption and is not an amplifier of postprandial colonic motility.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neither of these hormones is described as amplifying the postprandial increase in colonic motility.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Correct: gastrin and cholecystokinin amplify the gastrocolic reflex.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cholecystokinin does amplify the reflex, but aldosterone influences electrolyte and water absorption instead.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gastrin contributes to postprandial motility, but somatostatin is not part of this amplifying pair.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man undergoing anorectal testing is able to raise anal canal pressure abruptly and forcefully the instant he is asked to squeeze. Which of the following properties best explains this ability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The external anal sphincter is skeletal muscle under voluntary pudendal control

choices.label: B
choices.text: The internal anal sphincter is smooth muscle with high tonic autonomic tone

choices.label: C
choices.text: The internal anal sphincter receives direct corticospinal input from the motor cortex

choices.label: D
choices.text: The external anal sphincter is smooth muscle innervated by sympathetic hypogastric fibers

choices.label: E
choices.text: The taeniae coli contract tonically to raise anal canal pressure

explanation.summary: This item tests the composition and control of the external anal sphincter.
explanation.whyCorrect: The external anal sphincter is composed of skeletal (striated) muscle and forms a ring around the internal sphincter, so it is capable of rapid, forceful voluntary contraction. It is innervated by the somatic pudendal nerve (S2-S4), and cortical input by way of the corticospinal tract allows conscious contraction to maintain continence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Correct: skeletal muscle under somatic pudendal and cortical control can contract rapidly and forcefully on command.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tonic smooth muscle tone of the internal sphincter maintains resting pressure but cannot be increased at will.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cortical input reaches the external sphincter through the corticospinal tract and pudendal nerve; the internal sphincter is autonomically and enterically controlled.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The external sphincter is skeletal, not smooth, muscle, and the hypogastric nerve supplies the internal sphincter.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The taeniae coli generate tension along the colonic wall and have no role in anal canal pressure.

questions.stem: A physiologist separates the defecation reflex into its intrinsic and extrinsic components. Which of the following describes the extrinsic component of this reflex?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Myenteric plexus signaling that relaxes the internal anal sphincter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pudendal nerve firing that contracts the external anal sphincter

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypogastric sympathetic signaling that increases rectal contraction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sacral parasympathetic signaling that increases rectal peristalsis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vagal signaling that relaxes the external anal sphincter

explanation.summary: This item tests the extrinsic limb of the defecation reflex.
explanation.whyCorrect: The defecation reflex has an intrinsic component mediated by the enteric nervous system, which relaxes the internal anal sphincter through the rectoanal inhibitory reflex, and an extrinsic component mediated by sacral parasympathetic nerves (S2-S4). The extrinsic limb augments rectal contraction and increases rectal peristalsis after rectal distension.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Myenteric plexus mediated relaxation of the internal sphincter is the intrinsic component of the reflex, not the extrinsic one.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Contraction of the external sphincter is a somatic, voluntary act used to defer defecation rather than a limb of the reflex arc.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sympathetic hypogastric activity contracts the internal anal sphincter and supports continence.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Correct: sacral parasympathetic fibers (S2-S4) augment rectal contraction and peristalsis as the extrinsic component.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The external sphincter is skeletal muscle supplied by the pudendal nerve; it is not relaxed by vagal fibers.
